title.zh: 卷一百七十七 列傳第一百零二 錢崔二韋二高馮三李盧封鄭敬
title.en: Volume 177 Biographies 102: Qian, Cui, Two Wei's, Two Gao's, Feng, Three Li's, Lu, Feng, Zheng, Jing
title.raw: 卷一百七十七 列傳第一百零二 錢崔二韋二高馮三李盧封鄭敬 Volume 177 Biographies 102: Qian, Cui, Two Wei's, Two Gao's, Feng, Three Li's, Lu, Feng, Zheng, Jing

sentences.zh: 錢崔二韋二高馮三李盧封鄭敬

translations.literal: Qian, Cui, two Wei, two Gao, Feng, three Li, Lu, Feng, Zheng, Jing
translations.idiomatic: Qian, Cui, two men named Wei, two named Gao, Feng, three named Li, Lu, Feng, Zheng, and Jing

sentences.zh: 錢徽，字蔚章。

translations.literal: Qian Hui, courtesy name Weizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hui, whose courtesy name was Weizhang.

sentences.zh: 父起，附見《盧綸傳》。

translations.literal: His father Qi is treated in the biography of Lu Lun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi is discussed in the biography of Lu Lun.

sentences.zh: 徽中進士第，居谷城。

translations.literal: Hui passed the jinshi examination and lived in Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hui passed the jinshi examination and settled in Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 谷城令王郢善接僑士遊客，以財貸饋，坐是得罪。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Gucheng, Wang Ying, was good at receiving exiled scholars and travelers, lending and gifting them money and goods, for which he was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying, the magistrate of Gucheng, had a habit of hosting exiled scholars and itinerant guests, lending them money and gifts — an offense for which he was prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 觀察使樊澤視其簿，獨徽無有，乃表署掌書記。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner Fan Ze reviewed the registers; only Hui had nothing [recorded against him], so he memorialized to appoint him recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the observation commissioner Fan Ze examined the case records, he found that only Qian Hui was uninvolved, and therefore recommended him as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊方熾，澤多募武士於軍。

translations.literal: The Cai bandits were then at their height, and Ze recruited many warriors into the army.
translations.idiomatic: With the Cai rebels at the height of their power, Fan Ze recruited many fighting men into his forces.

sentences.zh: 澤卒，士頗希賞，周澈主留事，重擅發軍廥，不敢給。

translations.literal: When Ze died, the soldiers greatly hoped for rewards; Zhou Che oversaw remaining affairs and, because of repeatedly unauthorized issuance from the military granaries, dared not distribute [supplies].
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Ze died, the troops eagerly awaited rewards, but Zhou Che, who was left in charge, had repeatedly opened the army granaries without authorization and now dared not issue supplies.

sentences.zh: 時大雨雪，士寒凍，徽先冬頒衣絮，士乃大悅。

translations.literal: At the time heavy rain and snow fell; the soldiers were cold and freezing. Hui had previously distributed winter clothing and cotton in advance, and the soldiers were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow and bitter cold afflicted the troops; Hui had preemptively distributed winter clothing and padding the season before, and the men were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 又辟宣歙崔衍府。

translations.literal: He was again invited to the staff of Cui Yan of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: He was next invited to serve on the staff of Cui Yan, military governor of Xuan and She.

sentences.zh: 王師討蔡，檄遣采石兵會戰，戍還，頗驕蹇。

translations.literal: The imperial army campaigned against Cai; an edict dispatched the Chishi troops to join battle. When the garrison returned, they were quite arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial forces marched against Cai, an order sent the Chishi garrison to join the campaign; on their return the men were insolent and unruly.

sentences.zh: 會衍病亟，徽請召池州刺史李遜署副使，遜至而衍死，一軍賴以安。

translations.literal: When Yan fell gravely ill, Hui requested that Chi Prefecture prefect Li Xun be summoned to serve as deputy commissioner; Xun arrived and Yan died, and the whole army relied on this for stability.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yan fell gravely ill, Hui urged that Li Xun, prefect of Chi Prefecture, be appointed deputy commissioner; Li Xun arrived just as Yan died, and the army was spared chaos.

sentences.zh: 入拜左補闕，以祠部員外郎為翰林學士，三遷中書舍人，加承旨。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Left Remonstrator; as a member of the Secretariat in the post of Director of Rites, he became a Hanlin academician, was thrice promoted to Secretariat Drafter, and was given the additional title of Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Left Remonstrator, served as Hanlin academician while holding the post of Director of Rites in the Secretariat, was promoted three times to Secretariat Drafter, and was made Chief Academician.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘗獨召徽，從容言它學士皆高選，宜預聞機密，廣參決，帝稱其長者。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong once summoned Hui alone and, at ease, said that the other academicians were all highly selected and ought to be informed of secrets in advance and participate broadly in decisions; the emperor called him a man of mature judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong once received Hui in private audience and remarked, at his ease, that the other academicians were all men of exceptional selection and ought to be brought into confidential counsel and given a wider role in policy; the emperor praised him as a man of seasoned judgment.

sentences.zh: 是時，內積財，圖復河湟，然禁無名貢獻，而至者不甚卻。

translations.literal: At that time the court had amassed wealth and planned to recover Hexi, yet although unsolicited tribute was forbidden, arrivals were not much refused.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court had built up its treasury and planned to recover the Hexi region, and although unsolicited gifts were officially banned, those who brought them were seldom turned away.

sentences.zh: 徽懇諫罷之。

translations.literal: Hui earnestly remonstrated to abolish this.
translations.idiomatic: Hui earnestly urged the emperor to put an end to the practice.

sentences.zh: 帝密戒後有獻毋入右銀臺門，以避學士。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly warned that thereafter gifts should not enter the Right Silver Terrace Gate, so as to avoid the academicians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered that henceforth tribute bearers should not enter by the Right Silver Terrace Gate, so as to keep clear of the Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 梁守謙為院使，見徽批監軍表語簡約，嘆曰：「一字不可益邪！」

translations.literal: Liang Shouqian was commissioner of the academy; seeing Hui's endorsement on a supervisory-army memorial, concise in wording, he sighed and said: "Not a single character could be added, could it?"
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shouqian, commissioner of the Hanlin Academy, read Hui's endorsement on a memorial concerning army supervision — spare and exact — and exclaimed, "Not a single word could be added, could it?"

sentences.zh: 銜之。

translations.literal: He harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He bore a grudge against him from that day.

sentences.zh: 以論淮西事忤旨，罷職，徙太子右庶子，出虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Because in discussing the Huaixi campaign he offended the imperial will, he was removed from office, transferred to Right Vice-Gentleman of the Heir Apparent, and sent out as prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After his counsel on the Huaixi campaign ran counter to the emperor's wishes, he was dismissed from his post, made Right Vice-Gentleman of the Heir Apparent, and sent out as prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宰相段文昌以所善楊渾之、學士李紳以周漢賓並諉徽求致第籍。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Duan Wenchang, on behalf of his favorite Yang Hunzhi, and Academician Li Shen, on behalf of Zhou Hanbin, all pressed Hui to place them on the examination rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Duan Wenchang pressed him on behalf of his protégé Yang Hunzhi, and Hanlin academician Li Shen did the same for Zhou Hanbin, each asking that his man be passed.

sentences.zh: 渾之者憑子也，多納古帖秘畫於文昌，皆世所寶。

translations.literal: Hunzhi was the son of Feng, and had presented many ancient calligraphic scrolls and secret paintings to Wenchang, all treasures of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Hunzhi was the son of Feng and had lavished on Wenchang many ancient calligraphic scrolls and rare paintings, all objects prized throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 徽不能如二人請，自取楊殷士、蘇巢。

translations.literal: Hui could not comply with the two men's requests and himself selected Yang Yinshi and Su Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui could not grant what the two men asked and instead passed Yang Yinshi and Su Chao on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 巢者李宗閔婿，殷士者汝士之弟，皆與徽厚。

translations.literal: Chao was the son-in-law of Li Zongmin; Yinshi was the younger brother of Ru Shi; both were on close terms with Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was Li Zongmin's son-in-law and Yinshi was the younger brother of Ru Shi; both were intimate friends of Hui.

sentences.zh: 文昌怒，方帥劍南西川，入辭，即奏徽取士以私。

translations.literal: Wenchang was enraged; he was then military governor of Jiannan West and, on entering court to take leave, immediately memorialized that Hui had selected candidates out of private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang, furious, was at that time military governor of Jiannan West; when he came to court to take leave of the throne he immediately accused Hui of selecting candidates for private reasons.

sentences.zh: 訪紳及元稹，時稹與宗閔有隙，因是共擠其非。

translations.literal: He consulted Shen and Yuan Zhen; at the time Zhen and Zongmin were at odds, and on this account they jointly pressed charges of misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted Li Shen and Yuan Zhen; Zhen and Zongmin were then estranged, and the two men joined in denouncing Hui.

sentences.zh: 有詔王起、白居易覆試，而黜者過半，遂貶江州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wang Qi and Bai Juyi to conduct a re-examination; more than half were failed, and [Hui] was demoted to prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Qi and Bai Juyi to re-examine the candidates; more than half were failed, and Hui was demoted to prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 汝士等勸徽出文昌、紳私書自直，徽曰：「茍無愧於心，安事辨證邪？」

translations.literal: Ru Shi and others urged Hui to produce Wenchang's and Shen's private letters to clear himself; Hui said: "If one has no shame in one's heart, what need is there for argument and proof?"
translations.idiomatic: Ru Shi and others urged Hui to publish Wenchang's and Shen's private letters in his own defense; Hui replied, "If my conscience is clear, what need is there to argue the point?"

sentences.zh: 敕子弟焚書。

translations.literal: He ordered his sons and younger relatives to burn the letters.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his sons and nephews to burn the letters.

sentences.zh: 初，州有盜劫貢船，捕吏取濱江惡少年二百人系訊，徽按其枉，悉縱去。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the prefecture bandits had robbed a tribute ship; arresting officers seized two hundred wicked youths along the riverbank for interrogation. Hui investigated and found them innocent, and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, bandits in his prefecture had robbed a tribute vessel; the arresting officers had seized two hundred youths from along the river on suspicion. Hui found the charges baseless and released them all.

sentences.zh: 數日，舒州得真盜。

translations.literal: Within several days Shu Prefecture captured the real bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the real culprits were captured in Shu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州有牛田錢百萬，刺史以給宴飲贈餉者，徽曰：「此農耕之備，可他用哉！」

translations.literal: The prefecture had a million in ox-field funds that the prefect used for banquets, drinking, and gifts. Hui said: "These are reserves for farming — how can they be used for anything else?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture held a million cash in ox-field funds that previous prefects had spent on feasts and gifts; Hui declared, "These funds are meant for agriculture — how can they be diverted to other uses?"

sentences.zh: 命代貧民租入。

translations.literal: He ordered that they be used to pay the land tax for poor commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He applied them to pay the land tax for impoverished farmers.

sentences.zh: 轉湖州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 時宣、歙旱，左丞孔戣請徙徽領宣歙，宰相以其本文辭進，不用。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan and She suffered drought; Left Vice Director Kong Kan requested that Hui be moved to head Xuan and She. The chief ministers advanced his literary compositions and did not employ [the suggestion].
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan and She were stricken by drought, Left Vice Director Kong Kan urged that Hui be transferred to govern those circuits; the chief ministers cited his literary writings in support but the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 戣曰：「相君宜知天下事，徽江、虢之治不及知，況其它邪？」

translations.literal: Kan said: "The chief ministers ought to know affairs under heaven; they do not even know of Hui's governance in Jiang and Guo — how much less anything else?"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Kan retorted, "You chief ministers ought to know what is happening in the realm; you are unaware even of how Hui governed Jiang and Guo — what else do you fail to see?"

sentences.zh: 還，遷工部侍郎，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: He returned [to court], was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and was sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, promoted to Vice Minister of Works, and sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，召拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended, [Hui] was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, Hui was recalled and appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會宣墨麻，群臣在廷，方大寒，稍稍引避，徽素恭謹，不去位，久而仆。

translations.literal: When an imperial rescript was to be proclaimed, the assembled ministers were in court; it was bitterly cold, and they gradually withdrew. Hui, by nature respectful and cautious, did not leave his place, and after a long while collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: During the proclamation of an imperial rescript the ministers stood in court in bitter cold; one by one they withdrew. Hui, ever dutiful and careful, held his place until he finally collapsed.

sentences.zh: 因上疏告老，不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement on grounds of age; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial asking to retire on grounds of age, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 太和初，復為華州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign he again served in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign he returned to Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄以吏部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he retired as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired from office as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five and was posthumously given the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 徽與薛正倫、魏弘簡善，二人前死，徽撫其孤至婚嫁成立。

translations.literal: Hui was on good terms with Xue Zhenglun and Wei Hongjian; the two had died earlier, and Hui raised their orphans until marriage and establishment [in life] were accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had been close to Xue Zhenglun and Wei Hongjian; after both men died he raised their orphaned children until each was married and established in life.

sentences.zh: 任庶子時，韓公武以賂結公卿，遺徽錢二十萬，不納。

translations.literal: While serving as Vice-Gentleman of the Heir Apparent, Han Gongwu used bribes to win over the high ministers and sent Hui two hundred thousand in cash; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Vice-Gentleman of the Heir Apparent, Han Gongwu tried to buy influence among the high ministers and sent Hui two hundred thousand cash; Hui refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 或言非當路可無讓，徽曰：「取之在義不在官。」

translations.literal: Someone said that since he was not on the path of power he need not decline; Hui said: "Whether one may take lies in righteousness, not in office."
translations.idiomatic: When someone remarked that a man not in high office need not be so scrupulous, Hui replied, "What may be accepted depends on principle, not on rank."

sentences.zh: 時稱有公望。

translations.literal: At the time he was said to possess public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the day said he bore the marks of a statesman.

sentences.zh: 子可復、方義。

translations.literal: His sons were Kefu and Fangyi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Kefu and Fangyi.

sentences.zh: 可復死鄭註時。

translations.literal: Kefu died at the time of Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Kefu died during the Zheng Zhu affair.

sentences.zh: 方義終太子賓客。

translations.literal: Fangyi ended as Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyi ended his career as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子珝，字瑞文，善文辭，宰相王摶薦知制誥，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Xu, courtesy name Ruiwen, was skilled in literary composition; Chief Minister Wang Tuan recommended him as drafter of edicts, and he was advanced to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu, courtesy name Ruiwen, was gifted in letters; Chief Minister Wang Tuan recommended him as drafter of edicts, and he rose to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 搏得罪，珝貶撫州司馬。

translations.literal: Tuan fell from grace and Xu was demoted to military adjutant of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuan fell from power, Xu was demoted to military adjutant of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔鹹，字重易，博州博平人。

translations.literal: Cui Xian, courtesy name Chongyi, was a native of Boping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian, whose courtesy name was Chongyi, was a native of Boping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 元和初，擢進士第，又中宏辭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe reign he passed the jinshi examination and also passed the hongci examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he passed the jinshi examination and also won the hongci literary competition.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶、李夷簡皆表在幕府，與均禮。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing and Li Yijian both recommended him to their staffs and treated him with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing and Li Yijian both invited him onto their staffs and treated him with equal respect.

sentences.zh: 入朝為侍御史，處正特立，風采動一時。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attending Censor; upright and independent in conduct, his bearing stirred the age.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Attending Censor; upright and unyielding in principle, his bearing made a mark on his generation.

sentences.zh: 敬宗將幸東都，裴度在興元憂之，自表求覲，與章偕來。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong was about to visit the Eastern Capital; Pei Du, in Xingyuan, was troubled by this and submitted a memorial on his own requesting an audience, coming together with Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong planned a visit to the Eastern Capital, Pei Du, stationed at Xingyuan, was alarmed and memorialized on his own requesting an audience at court, arriving together with Zhang.

sentences.zh: 於是李逢吉當國，畏度復相，使京兆尹劉棲楚等十餘人悉力拫卻之，雖度門下賓客，皆有去就意。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Fengji held power and, fearing that Du would again become chief minister, had more than ten men including the metropolitan prefect Liu Qichu exert all their strength to repel and obstruct him; even among guests at Du's gate there were those who considered leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji was then in control of the government and, fearing that Pei Du might return as chief minister, set more than a dozen men led by the metropolitan prefect Liu Qichu to work blocking him at every turn; even among the guests at Pei Du's door some began to think of leaving.

sentences.zh: 它日，度置酒延客，棲楚曲意自解，附耳語。

translations.literal: Another day Du set out wine and entertained guests; Qichu bent his intentions to make amends and spoke into his ear.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Pei Du gave a banquet for his guests; Liu Qichu tried to ingratiate himself and whispered in his ear.

sentences.zh: 鹹嫉其矯，舉酒讓度曰：「丞相乃許所由官囁嚅耳語，願上罰爵。」

translations.literal: Xian resented his affectation; raising his cup he rebuked Du, saying: "The chief minister actually permits a petty official to whisper in his ear — I ask that you be fined a cup."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian, disgusted by the display, raised his cup and rebuked Pei Du: "The chief minister allows a petty official to whisper in his ear — I ask that you drain a penalty cup."

sentences.zh: 度笑受而飲。

translations.literal: Du smiled, accepted, and drank.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du smiled, accepted the rebuke, and drank.

sentences.zh: 棲楚不自安，趨出，坐上莫不壯之。

translations.literal: Qichu was ill at ease and hurried out; none at the table failed to admire [Xian].
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu, mortified, hurried from the hall; everyone present admired Cui Xian's boldness.

sentences.zh: 累遷陜虢觀察使，日與賓客僚屬痛飲，未嘗醒；

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to observation commissioner of Shan and Guo; by day he drank heavily with guests and subordinates and was never sober;
translations.idiomatic: He rose to observation commissioner of Shan and Guo, where he drank heavily every day with guests and staff and was never sober;

sentences.zh: 夜分輒決事，裁剖精明，無一毫差，吏稱為神。

translations.literal: at midnight he would decide affairs; his judgments were keen and precise, without the slightest error, and the clerks called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: yet at midnight he would settle official business with keen and exact judgment, never erring by a hair, and his clerks called him uncanny.

sentences.zh: 入拜右散騎常侍、秘書監。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Right Regular Attendant and Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Right Regular Attendant and Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 太和八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of the Taihe reign.

sentences.zh: 鹹素有高世誌，造詣嶄遠。

translations.literal: Xian had long cherished lofty ambitions beyond the age; his attainments were steep and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had long cherished ambitions that rose above his age; his learning was profound and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 間遊終南山，乘月吟嘯，至感慨泣下。

translations.literal: He would from time to time roam Zhongnan Mountain, chanting and whistling by moonlight, until moved to tears by emotion.
translations.idiomatic: He would wander Zhongnan Mountain, chanting and calling under the moon until he was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 諸文中歌詩最善。

translations.literal: Among his writings songs and poetry were best.
translations.idiomatic: Of all his writings, his songs and poems were finest.

sentences.zh: 韋表微，字子明，隋郿城公元禮七世孫。

translations.literal: Wei Biaowei, courtesy name Ziming, was seventh-generation descendant of Yuan Li, Duke of Meicheng of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Biaowei, whose courtesy name was Ziming, was a seventh-generation descendant of Yuan Li, Duke of Meicheng of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 羈能屬文。

translations.literal: While still young he could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 母訓諭稍厲，輒不敢食，以是未嘗讓責。

translations.literal: When his mother's instruction and admonition grew somewhat stern, he would at once refuse to eat; on this account she never had to reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his mother's admonitions grew stern he would refuse his meal at once, and for that reason she never needed to chide him.

sentences.zh: 韋臯鎮西川，王緯、司空曙、獨孤良弼、裴涚居幕府，皆厚相推挹。

translations.literal: When Wei Gao governed Xichuan, Wang Wei, Sikong Shu, Dugu Liangbi, and Pei Shui served in his staff; all warmly promoted and lifted [Biaowei] up.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Gao governed the West Circuit, Wang Wei, Sikong Shu, Dugu Liangbi, and Pei Shui served on his staff and all warmly championed Biaowei.

sentences.zh: 涚嘗謂表微似衛玠，自以不能及也。

translations.literal: Shui once said that Biaowei resembled Wei Jie and that he himself could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shui once remarked that Biaowei resembled Wei Jie in bearing and confessed that he himself could not equal him.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，數辟諸使府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited to various commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited onto the staffs of various commissioners.

sentences.zh: 久之，入授監察御史裏行，不樂，曰：「爵祿譬滋味也，人皆欲之。

translations.literal: After a long while he entered court and was given the post of Acting Investigating Censor; he was not pleased and said: "Rank and salary are like flavors — everyone wants them.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he entered the capital and was appointed Acting Investigating Censor, a post he did not relish; he said, "Rank and salary are like flavors — everyone craves them.

sentences.zh: 吾年五十，拭鏡揃白，冒遊少年間，取一班一級，不見其味也。

translations.literal: I am fifty years old, wiping the mirror and trimming white hair, mingling among youths to seize one grade and one rank — I do not taste the flavor.
translations.idiomatic: I am fifty, wiping my mirror and trimming my white hairs, mingling among young men to win one more grade and rank — and I taste nothing in it.

sentences.zh: 將為松菊主人，不愧陶淵明」雲。

translations.literal: I shall become master of pines and chrysanthemums and not be shamed before Tao Yuanming," he said.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to be master of pines and chrysanthemums and hold my head up before Tao Yuanming," he declared.

sentences.zh: 俄為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he became a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 是時，李紳忤宰相，貶端州，龐嚴、蔣防皆謫去，學士缺，人人爭薦丞相所善者，表微獨薦韋處厚，人服其公。

translations.literal: At that time Li Shen had offended the chief minister and was demoted to Duan Prefecture; Pang Yan and Jiang Fang were both banished and removed; the academicians were short, and everyone contended to recommend those favored by the chief minister. Biaowei alone recommended Wei Chuhou, and men admired his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Shen had crossed the chief minister and was banished to Duan Prefecture; Pang Yan and Jiang Fang had also been sent away, leaving vacancies among the academicians. Everyone scrambled to recommend the chief minister's favorites, but Biaowei alone nominated Wei Chuhou, and men admired his impartiality.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥。

translations.literal: He was advanced to drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 後與處厚議增選學士，復薦路隋。

translations.literal: Later, discussing with Chuhou the addition of selected academicians, he again recommended Lu Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he and Chuhou discussed adding new academicians, he again recommended Lu Sui.

sentences.zh: 處厚以諸父事表微，因曰：「隋位崇，入且翁右，奈何？」

translations.literal: Chuhou treated Biaowei as an uncle by the father's line and therefore said: "Sui's rank is lofty; when he enters he will be to your right as senior — what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou, who regarded Biaowei as an uncle, objected: "Sui outranks you; when he joins us he will sit to your right as the senior — how can that be?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「選德進賢，初不計私也。」

translations.literal: He answered: "In selecting the virtuous and advancing the worthy, from the first one does not reckon private ties."
translations.idiomatic: Biaowei replied, "In choosing men of virtue and talent one does not count private ties from the start."

sentences.zh: 久之，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嘗語左右，欲相二韋，會崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong once told those around him that he wished to make both Wei men chief ministers, but he happened to die.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong once told his attendants that he meant to make both Wei men chief ministers, but he died before he could do so.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，獨相處厚，進表微戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended, he alone made Chuhou chief minister and advanced Biaowei to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne he made Chuhou sole chief minister and promoted Biaowei to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 丌誌沼叛，詔李聽率師討之，次河上。

translations.literal: Qi Zhizhao rebelled; an edict ordered Li Ting to lead troops to campaign against him, halting on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Zhizhao rebelled, an edict ordered Li Ting to lead an army against him, and the force halted on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 天子憂無成功，表微曰：「以聽軍勢，不十五日必破賊。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven worried that there would be no success; Biaowei said: "Given Ting's military strength, within fifteen days the bandits will surely be broken."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared the campaign would fail; Biaowei said, "Given the strength of Li Ting's army, the rebels will be broken within fifteen days."

sentences.zh: 及捷書上，止浹日。

translations.literal: When the victory report arrived, it was only ten days.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory dispatch arrived, only ten days had passed.

sentences.zh: 誌沼殘兵六千奔昭義，宰相請推處首惡者誅之，歸脅從者於魏。

translations.literal: Zhizhao's remnant force of six thousand fled to Zhaoyi; the chief ministers requested that the ringleaders be identified and executed and the coerced followers returned to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhao's six thousand remaining troops fled to Zhaoyi; the chief ministers proposed identifying the ringleaders for execution and sending the coerced followers back to Wei.

sentences.zh: 表微上言：「逆子降，又殺之，非好生也。

translations.literal: Biaowei submitted a memorial saying: "Rebellious sons who have surrendered — to kill them again is not cherishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Biaowei memorialized: "To put surrendered rebels to death is not the way of a ruler who cherishes life.

sentences.zh: 請以聽代史憲誠於魏，誌沼之徒，可使招納。」

translations.literal: I request that Ting replace Shi Xianchéng in Wei; Zhizhao's followers may be induced to submit."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that Li Ting replace Shi Xianchéng in Wei and that Zhizhao's followers be induced to surrender."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not heed [this].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his counsel.

sentences.zh: 以病痼罷學士。

translations.literal: Because of a chronic illness he was removed from the academy.
translations.idiomatic: A chronic illness forced him to leave the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty and was posthumously given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty and was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 始，被病，醫藥不能具，所居堂寢隘陋，既沒，吊客咨嗟。

translations.literal: From the first, when he fell ill, medicine could not be fully provided; the hall and sleeping quarters where he lived were cramped and shabby; after he died, mourners sighed in lament.
translations.idiomatic: From the first, when illness struck him, he lacked adequate medicine; his hall and bedchamber were cramped and mean; after his death mourners sighed at the sight.

sentences.zh: 篤故舊，雖庸下，與攜手語笑無間然。

translations.literal: He was devoted to old friends; even the lowly he joined hand in hand in speech and laughter without interval.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to old friends; even with the humblest he would join hands in talk and laughter without reserve.

sentences.zh: 尤好《春秋》，病諸儒執一概，是非紛然，著《三傳總例》，完會經趣。

translations.literal: He especially loved the Spring and Autumn Annals; he faulted the scholars for holding to one uniform standard with right and wrong in confusion, and wrote Comprehensive Patterns of the Three Commentaries, completing the meeting of the classic's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to the Spring and Autumn Annals; he deplored scholars who clung to a single rigid standard while right and wrong remained tangled, and wrote Comprehensive Patterns of the Three Commentaries to restore the classic's full meaning.

sentences.zh: 又以學者薄師道，不如聲樂賤工能尊其師，著《九經師授譜》詆其違。

translations.literal: He also [noted] that scholars slighted the way of teachers, not like music's base craftsmen who can honor their teachers, and wrote 《Register of Nine Classics Master-Disciple Transmission》 to denounce their violations.
translations.idiomatic: He also deplored that scholars held teachers in contempt, unlike even the humblest musicians and artisans who honor their masters, and wrote the 《Register of Nine Classics Master-Disciple Transmission》 to condemn their breach of that duty.

sentences.zh: 高釴，字翹之，史失其何所人。

translations.literal: Gao Yi, courtesy name Qiaozhi—the histories do not record where he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yi, courtesy name Qiaozhi, was a man whose native place the histories have lost.

sentences.zh: 與弟銖、鍇俱擢進士第。

translations.literal: He together with his younger brothers Zhu and Kai all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brothers Zhu and Kai all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷右補闕、史館脩撰。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor and Drafting Compiler in the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Right Remonstrance Censor and Drafting Compiler in the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 元和末，以中人為和糴使，釴繼疏論執。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era, because eunuchs were made grain-purchase commissioners, Yi repeatedly submitted memorials arguing against it.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanhe era, when eunuchs were appointed grain-purchase commissioners, Yi submitted memorial after memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 轉起居郎，數陳政得失，穆宗嘉之，面賜緋、魚，召入翰林，為學士。

translations.literal: He transferred to Diarist of the Left, often setting forth the merits and faults of government; Muzong commended him, personally bestowing crimson robes and the fish tally, and summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as an Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Diarist of the Left, he repeatedly laid out what was right and wrong in government; Emperor Muzong praised him, personally bestowed crimson robes and the fish tally, and summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as an Academician.

sentences.zh: 張韶變興倉卒，釴從敬宗夜駐左軍。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shao's mutiny arose hastily, Yi followed Jingzong and encamped overnight at the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shao's mutiny broke out suddenly, Yi accompanied Emperor Jingzong and spent the night encamped with the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 翌日，進知制誥，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: The next day he was promoted to Drafter of Proclamations and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he was promoted to Drafter of Proclamations and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 入見帝，因勸躬聽掔以示憂勤，帝納其言，賜錦彩。

translations.literal: Upon entering to see the Emperor, he urged him to personally listen to state affairs to show concern and diligence; the Emperor accepted his words and bestowed brocade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered to see the Emperor, he urged him to attend personally to affairs of state as a sign of devoted concern; the Emperor took his advice and rewarded him with brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 俄罷學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed from the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was removed from the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 累進吏部侍郎，人善其振職。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel; people praised his invigorating of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted step by step to Vice Minister of Personnel, he was admired for the vigor with which he discharged his duties.

sentences.zh: 出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部尚書，遺命薄葬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Minister of War; his final testament ordered a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Minister of War; his dying instructions called for a plain burial.

sentences.zh: 釴少孤窶，介然無黨援，以致宦達。

translations.literal: Yi was orphaned and poor in youth, stood apart without factional backing, yet attained official eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, Yi stood apart from factions and without patronage, yet still rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 諸弟皆檢願友愛，為搢紳景重。

translations.literal: All his younger brothers were restrained, virtuous, and affectionate, and were admired and respected among the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: All his younger brothers were self-restrained, virtuous, and devoted to one another, and were held in high esteem among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 子湜，字澄之，第進士，累官右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His son Mi, courtesy name Chengzhi, passed the jinshi examination and cumulatively served to Right Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi, courtesy name Chengzhi, passed the jinshi examination and rose through the ranks to Right Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 咸通末，為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiantong era, he served as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xiantong era he served as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時士多繇權要幹請，湜不能裁，既而抵帽於地曰：「吾決以至公取之，得譴固吾分！」

translations.literal: At the time many candidates obtained favor through powerful patrons' intercession; Mi could not restrain it, and finally threw his hat to the ground, saying: "I am resolved to select them by utmost fairness; if I incur censure, that is simply my lot!"
translations.idiomatic: At the time many candidates gained entry through petitions from the powerful, and Mi could not check the practice; finally he threw his hat to the floor and said, "I am determined to choose men by absolute fairness—even if I am punished for it, that is only what I deserve!"

sentences.zh: 乃取公乘億、許棠、聶夷中等。

translations.literal: Accordingly he selected Gongcheng Yi, Xu Tang, Nie Yizhong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected Gongcheng Yi, Xu Tang, Nie Yizhong, and others.

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎判度支出為昭義節度使，為下所逐，貶連州司馬。

translations.literal: As Vice Minister of War concurrently overseeing the Salt and Grain Commission, he went out as military governor of Zhaoyi; driven out by his subordinates, he was demoted to prefectural aide of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Vice Minister of War with concurrent charge of the Salt and Grain Commission, he was sent out as military governor of Zhaoyi; his subordinates drove him out, and he was demoted to prefectural aide of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 以太子賓客分司東都，卒。

translations.literal: Appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital, he died there.

sentences.zh: 億字壽仙，棠字文化，夷中字坦之，皆有名當時。

translations.literal: Yi had courtesy name Shouxian, Tang had Wenhua, Yizhong had Tanzhi—all were renowned at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Gongcheng Yi, courtesy name Shouxian; Xu Tang, courtesy name Wenhua; and Nie Yizhong, courtesy name Tanzhi—all were celebrated men of their day.

sentences.zh: 銖，字權仲，既擢第，署太原張弘靖幕府，入遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Zhu, courtesy name Quanzhong, after passing the examination was appointed to the staff of Zhang Hongjing in Taiyuan; entering the capital he was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, courtesy name Quanzhong, after passing the examination joined the staff of Zhang Hongjing in Taiyuan; on entering the capital he was promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 太和時，擢累給事中。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era he was promoted cumulatively to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he rose through successive promotions to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 文宗得李訓，驟拜侍講學士，銖率諫官伏閣言訓素行憸邪，不可任，必亂天下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong obtained Li Xun and suddenly appointed him Lecturing Academician, Zhu led the remonstrance officials in kneeling at the palace gate to say Xun's conduct had long been treacherous and wicked, that he could not be entrusted with office and would surely bring chaos upon the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took up with Li Xun and abruptly appointed him Lecturing Academician, Zhu led the remonstrance officials in kneeling at the palace gate to declare that Xun's character had long been treacherous and corrupt, that he must not be entrusted with office, and that he would surely throw the realm into chaos.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者諭曰：「朕留訓時時講繹，前命不可改。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a messenger to instruct them: "I keep Xun to expound the classics from time to time; the prior appointment cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a messenger to tell them, "I keep Xun here to expound the classics from time to time; the appointment already made cannot be revoked."

sentences.zh: 當是時，已旱而水，彗變未息，鄭註權震赫，人情危駭，既銖等弗見省，群臣失色。

translations.literal: At that time there had already been drought yet also flooding, comet portents had not ceased, Zheng Zhu's power blazed forth, and people's hearts were gripped by fear; when Zhu and the others received no heed, the officials turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: At that time drought and flood had already struck in turn, comet portents had not subsided, Zheng Zhu's power blazed unchecked, and the people lived in dread; when Zhu and his colleagues went unheard, the court officials turned pale.

sentences.zh: 明年，訓當國，出銖為浙東觀察使，歷義成節度使。

translations.literal: The next year, when Xun held power, Zhu was sent out as governor of Zhedong; he later served as military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, once Xun held the reins of government, Zhu was sent out as governor of Zhedong and later served as military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 大中初，遷禮部尚書判戶部，徙太常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era he was transferred to Minister of Rites concurrently overseeing the Ministry of Revenue, then moved to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Dazhong era he was transferred to Minister of Rites with concurrent charge of the Ministry of Revenue, then moved to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嘗罰禮生，博士李愨慍見曰：「故事，禮院不關白太常，故卿蒞職，博士不參集。

translations.literal: Once he punished a ritual clerk; Doctor of Rites Li Nu came before him in anger and said: "By precedent the Ritual Academy does not report to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; therefore when you took office the doctors did not assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Once he punished a ritual clerk; Doctor of Rites Li Nu came before him in anger and said, "By established practice the Ritual Academy does not report to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, so when you took office the doctors did not assemble.

sentences.zh: 不宜罰小史，隳舊典。」

translations.literal: One ought not punish a minor clerk and destroy old institutions."
translations.idiomatic: You ought not punish a minor clerk and overturn long-standing precedent."

sentences.zh: 銖嘆曰：「吾老不能退，乃為小兒所辱！」

translations.literal: Zhu sighed and said: "I am old and cannot retire, yet am insulted by a youngster!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu sighed and said, "I am old and cannot bring myself to retire, yet here I am insulted by a stripling!"

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 鍇，字弱金，連中進士、宏辭科，辟河東府參謀，歷吏部員外郎，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Ruojin, consecutively passed the jinshi and the Hongci examinations; he was recruited as staff officer of the Hedong commandery, served as Vice Director of Personnel, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, courtesy name Ruojin, passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations in succession; he entered the staff of the Hedong commandery, served as Vice Director of Personnel, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng he served as acting director of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Kaicheng era he served as acting director of the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 文宗自以題畀有司，鍇以籍上，帝語侍臣曰：「比年文章卑弱，今所上差勝於前。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong himself had set the examination topics and handed them to the officials; when Kai submitted the registry, the Emperor said to his attendant ministers: "In recent years examinees' compositions have been feeble; what is submitted now is somewhat better than before."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong himself set the examination topics and handed them to the officials; when Kai submitted the roster of candidates, the Emperor told his attendant ministers, "In recent years the essays have been weak; what has been submitted now is somewhat better than before."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「陛下矯革近制，以正頹俗，而鍇乃能為陛下得人。」

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Your Majesty has reformed recent regulations to rectify a declining custom, and Kai has been able to obtain men for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, "Your Majesty has reformed recent practice to set right a declining custom, and Kai has been able to find worthy men for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諸鎮表奏太浮華，宜責掌書記，以誡流宕。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The memorials from the various prefectures are too ornate; the record-keepers should be held responsible, to warn against excess and frivolity."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The memorials from the various circuits are too florid; their chief secretaries should be held accountable, as a warning against empty extravagance."

sentences.zh: 李石曰：「古人因事為文，今人以文害事，懲弊抑末，誠如聖訓。」

translations.literal: Li Shi said: "The ancients wrote according to affairs; today men let writing harm affairs—to punish abuse and restrain the secondary, truly accords with Your Majesty's teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi said, "The ancients wrote to serve affairs; today men let writing obstruct affairs. To punish abuse and restrain what is secondary truly accords with Your Majesty's instruction."

sentences.zh: 即以鍇為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Kai was thereupon appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was thereupon appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 閱三歲，頗得才實。

translations.literal: After three years he had obtained quite a number of men of real talent.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years he secured a good many candidates of genuine ability.

sentences.zh: 始，歲取四十人，才益少，詔減十人，猶不能滿。

translations.literal: At first forty men were taken each year, but talent grew ever scarcer; an edict reduced the quota by ten, yet they still could not fill it.
translations.idiomatic: At first forty men were selected each year, but worthy talent grew ever scarcer; an edict cut the quota by ten, yet even then the places could not be filled.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，出為鄂嶽觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and went out as governor of E-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and sent out as governor of E-Yue.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子湘，字濬之，擢進士第，歷長安令、右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, courtesy name Junzhi, passed the jinshi examination and served successively as magistrate of Chang'an and Right Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang, courtesy name Junzhi, passed the jinshi examination and served in turn as magistrate of Chang'an and Right Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 從兄湜與路巖親善，而湘厚劉瞻，巖既逐瞻，貶湘高州司馬。

translations.literal: His cousin Mi was close to Lu Yan, while Xiang was deeply attached to Liu Zhan; when Yan had already driven out Zhan, Xiang was demoted to prefectural aide of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Mi was on close terms with Lu Yan, while Xiang was deeply attached to Liu Zhan; after Yan had driven Zhan out, Xiang was demoted to prefectural aide of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗初，召為太子右庶子，終江西觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xizong's reign he was summoned as Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and ended his career as governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xizong's reign he was recalled as Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and ended his career as governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 馮宿，字拱之，婺州東陽人。

translations.literal: Feng Su, courtesy name Gongzhi, was a native of Dongyang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Su, courtesy name Gongzhi, was a native of Dongyang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父子華，廬親墓，有靈芝、白兔，號「孝馮家」。

translations.literal: Su and his father Zihua kept vigil at their parents' tomb; there appeared spirit fungus and white hares, and they were called "the Filial Feng family."
translations.idiomatic: Su and his father Zihua kept vigil at their parents' tomb; spirit fungus and white hares appeared there, and they were known as "the Filial Feng family."

sentences.zh: 宿貞元中與弟定、從弟審、寬並擢進士第，徐州張建封表掌書記。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era Su together with his brother Ding and his cousins Shen and Kuan all passed the jinshi examination; Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou submitted a memorial appointing him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era Su, together with his brother Ding and his cousins Shen and Kuan, all passed the jinshi examination; Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 建封卒，子愔為軍中脅主留事。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng died, his son Yin was coerced by the army to take charge of affairs as acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng died, his son Yin was forced by the army to take charge of affairs as acting commander.

sentences.zh: 李師古將乘喪復故地，愔大懼。

translations.literal: Li Shigu was about to seize the interval of mourning to recover former territory; Yin was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu was about to exploit the mourning period to recover lost territory, and Yin was terrified.

sentences.zh: 於是，王武俊擁兵觀釁，宿以書說曰：「張公與公為兄弟，欲共力驅兩河歸天子，天下莫不知。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Wujun massed troops watching for an opening; Su wrote to persuade him, saying: "Lord Zhang and you were as brothers, wishing together to drive the Two He regions back to the Son of Heaven—no one under Heaven does not know this.
translations.idiomatic: At that point Wang Wujun gathered his troops and watched for an opening; Su wrote to persuade him, saying, "Lord Zhang and you stood as brothers, resolved together to drive the Two He regions back to the Son of Heaven—the whole realm knows it.

sentences.zh: 今張公不幸，幼兒為亂兵所脅，內則誠款隔絕，外則強寇侵逼，公安得坐視哉？

translations.literal: Now Lord Zhang has met misfortune; the young son is coerced by mutinous troops—within, sincere good faith is cut off; without, strong enemies press in—how can you sit and watch?
translations.idiomatic: Now Lord Zhang has met with misfortune; his young son is held hostage by mutinous troops—cut off within from loyal submission, pressed from without by powerful foes—how can you stand by and do nothing?

sentences.zh: 誠能奏天子不忘舊勛，赦愔罪，使束身自歸，則公有靖亂之功、繼絕之德矣。」

translations.literal: If you can truly memorialize the Son of Heaven not to forget old merit, pardon Yin's offense, and cause him to restrain himself and return in submission, then you will have the merit of quelling disorder and the virtue of continuing what was broken off."
translations.idiomatic: If you will truly memorialize the Son of Heaven not to forget past service, pardon Yin's offense, and bring him to submit of his own accord, you will earn the credit of quelling disorder and the virtue of preserving a line that would otherwise be cut off."

sentences.zh: 武俊悅，即以表聞，遂授愔留後。

translations.literal: Wujun was pleased, immediately submitted a memorial reporting this, and Yin was thereupon appointed acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was pleased, submitted a memorial at once, and Yin was thereupon appointed acting commander.

sentences.zh: 宿不樂佐愔，更從浙東賈全觀察府。

translations.literal: Su did not wish to serve under Yin and instead joined the staff of Jia Quan, governor of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: Su had no wish to serve under Yin and instead joined the staff of Jia Quan, governor of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 愔憾其去，奏貶泉州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Yin resented his departure and memorialized to demote him to military aide of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin resented his leaving and memorialized to have him demoted to military aide of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為太常博士。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王士真死，子承宗阻命，不得謚，宿謂世勞不可遺，乃上佳謚，示不忘忠。

translations.literal: When Wang Shizhen died, his son Chengzong defied orders and no posthumous title was granted; Su held that merits earned in the world could not be cast aside, and so submitted a fine posthumous title to show that loyalty was not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shizhen died, his son Chengzong defied the court and no posthumous title was granted; Su held that lifetime service could not be cast aside, and so submitted a worthy posthumous title to show that loyalty was not forgotten.

sentences.zh: 再遷都官員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Office of Judgment Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Office of Judgment Review.

sentences.zh: 裴度節度彰義軍，表為判官。

translations.literal: Pei Du, as military governor of Zhangyi, submitted a memorial appointing him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du served as military governor of Zhangyi, he memorialized to appoint Su as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 淮西平，除比部郎中。

translations.literal: When Huai West was pacified, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai West was pacified, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 長慶時，進知制誥。

translations.literal: During the Changqing era he was promoted to Drafter of Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era he was promoted to Drafter of Proclamations.

sentences.zh: 牛元翼徙節山南東道，為王廷湊所圍，以宿總留事。

translations.literal: When Niu Yuanji was transferred to govern Shannan East Circuit and was besieged by Wang Tingcou, Su was left in charge of overall affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Yuanji was transferred to govern Shannan East Circuit and was besieged by Wang Tingcou, Su was left in overall charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 還，進中書舍人，出華州刺史，避諱不拜，徙左散騎常侍、兼集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Upon return he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and sent out as prefect of Huazhou; to avoid a taboo name he declined the appointment and was transferred to Left Palace Companion and concurrent Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and sent out as prefect of Huazhou; to avoid a taboo name he declined the post and was transferred to Left Palace Companion and concurrent Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 拜河南尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 洛苑使姚文壽縱部曲奪民田，匿於軍，吏不敢捕。

translations.literal: The Luoyang Park commissioner Yao Wenshou let his troops seize commoners' fields and hid them within the army; officials dared not arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang Park commissioner Yao Wenshou let his retainers seize commoners' fields and sheltered them within the army, and officials dared not arrest them.

sentences.zh: 府大集，部曲輒與文壽偕來，宿掩取榜殺之。

translations.literal: When the prefectural offices held a general assembly, the troops came together with Wenshou; Su had them seized on the spot and beaten to death on the posting board.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectural offices held a general assembly, the retainers came together with Wenshou; Su had them seized on the spot and beaten to death at the public posting board.

sentences.zh: 歷工部、刑部二侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Public Works and Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Vice Minister of Public Works and Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 脩《格後敕》三十篇，行於時。

translations.literal: He compiled thirty chapters of 《Supplemental Edicts After the Code of Statutes》, which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled thirty chapters of the 《Supplemental Edicts After the Code of Statutes》, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 累封長樂縣公。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed, ultimately as Duke of Changle County.

sentences.zh: 擢東川節度使，完城郛，增兵械十餘萬，詔分余甲賜黔巫道。

translations.literal: Promoted as military governor of Dongchuan, he completed the walls and ramparts and increased armaments by more than a hundred thousand; an edict apportioned surplus armor to the Qian-Wu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to military governor of Dongchuan, he completed the walls and ramparts and increased armaments by more than a hundred thousand pieces; an edict ordered surplus armor distributed to the Qian-Wu circuit.

sentences.zh: 涪水數壞民廬舍，宿脩利防庸，一方便賴。

translations.literal: The Fu River repeatedly destroyed commoners' houses; Su repaired flood-control works and labor corvée, to the great benefit of the whole region.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu River repeatedly destroyed commoners' dwellings; Su repaired flood-control works and labor corvée, and the whole region benefited.

sentences.zh: 疾革，將斷重刑，家人請宥之，宿曰：「命脩短，天也。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, he was about to impose a heavy sentence; his family asked that the offender be pardoned; Su said: "Whether life is long or short is Heaven's doing.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned critical, he was about to impose a heavy sentence; his family asked that the offender be pardoned, and Su said, "Whether life is long or short is Heaven's decree.

sentences.zh: 撓法以求祐，吾不敢。」

translations.literal: To bend the law seeking blessing—I dare not."
translations.idiomatic: To bend the law in hope of divine favor—I dare not."

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十，贈吏部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy; posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel; posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy, was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel, and was given the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 治命薄葬，悉以平生書納墓中。

translations.literal: His final testament ordered a simple burial and that all his life's writings be placed in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His dying instructions called for a plain burial and for all his writings to be placed in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 子圖，字昌之，連中進士、宏辭科。

translations.literal: His son Tu, courtesy name Changzhi, consecutively passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tu, courtesy name Changzhi, passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations in succession.

sentences.zh: 大中時，終戶部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong era he ended as Vice Minister of Revenue concurrently overseeing the Salt and Grain Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era he ended his career as Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of the Salt and Grain Commission.

sentences.zh: 寬為起居郎。

translations.literal: Kuan served as Diarist of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan served as Diarist of the Left.

sentences.zh: 定，字介夫，偉儀觀，與宿齊名，人方漢二馮。

translations.literal: Ding, courtesy name Jiefu, had a lofty bearing; he was equally famous with Su, and people compared them to the two Fengs of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ding, courtesy name Jiefu, had a commanding presence; he was as renowned as Su, and people compared the two to the two Fengs of Han.

sentences.zh: 於頔素善之。

translations.literal: Yu Di had long favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di had long been well disposed toward him.

sentences.zh: 頔在襄陽，定徒步上謁，吏不肯白，乃亟去。

translations.literal: When Di was at Xiangyang, Ding came on foot to call on him; the gate officer refused to announce him, and he promptly left.
translations.idiomatic: When Di was at Xiangyang, Ding came on foot to pay a call; the gate officer refused to announce him, and Ding left at once.

sentences.zh: 頔聞，斥吏，歸錢五十萬，及諸境，定返其遺，以書讓頔不下士，頔大慚。

translations.literal: When Di heard of it he rebuked the officer and sent back five hundred thousand cash; when Ding reached the border he returned the gift and wrote a letter reproaching Di for not humbling himself before scholars; Di was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: When Di heard of it he rebuked the officer and sent after Ding with five hundred thousand cash; at the border Ding returned the gift and wrote reproaching Di for failing to humble himself before scholars, and Di was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 第進士異等，辟浙西薛蘋府，以鄠尉為集賢校理。

translations.literal: Passing the jinshi at a distinguished grade, he entered the staff of Xue Pin in Zhexi; as aide of E County he served as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the jinshi at a distinguished grade, he entered the staff of Xue Pin in Zhexi; while serving as aide of E County he was also collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 始，定居喪，號毀甚，故數移疾，大學士疑其簡怠，奪職。

translations.literal: At first, while dwelling in mourning, he grieved so severely that he repeatedly requested leave on grounds of illness; a Grand Academician suspected him of neglect and stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while in mourning, he grieved so severely that he repeatedly asked leave on grounds of illness; a Grand Academician suspected neglect and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 三遷祠部員外郎，出為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and went out as prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and was sent out as prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 吏告定略民妻，乾沒庫錢，御史鞫治無狀。

translations.literal: An official reported that Ding had abducted a commoner's wife and embezzled treasury funds; the censor investigated and found no basis.
translations.idiomatic: An official reported that Ding had seized a commoner's wife and embezzled treasury funds; the censor investigated and found no substance to the charges.

sentences.zh: 坐遊宴不節免官。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for unrestrained feasting and revelry.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office for unrestrained feasting and revelry.

sentences.zh: 起為國子司業，再遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was reappointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and after two promotions became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and, after two further promotions, became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 文宗嘗詔開元《霓裳羽衣舞》參以《雲韶》，肄於廷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong once ordered the Kaiyuan era 《Robe of Feathers and Colored Skirts Dance》 to be combined with the 《Cloud Auspice Music》 and rehearsed in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong once ordered the Kaiyuan-era 《Robe of Feathers and Colored Skirts Dance》 to be combined with the 《Cloud Auspice Music》 and rehearsed in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 定部諸工立縣間，端凝若植。

translations.literal: Ding organized the various performers standing at intervals, upright and solemn as planted posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ding arranged the performers standing at intervals, upright and solemn as though planted in place.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，問學士李玨，玨以定對。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at it and asked Academician Li Jue, who answered in Ding's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marveled at it and asked Academician Li Jue, who answered on Ding's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「豈非能古章句者邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "Is this not one who understands ancient commentaries?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said with pleasure, "Is this not a man versed in the old commentaries?"

sentences.zh: 親誦定《送客西江》詩，召升殿，賜禁中瑞錦，詔悉所著以上。

translations.literal: He personally recited Ding's poem 《Seeing Off a Guest on the Western River》, summoned him to ascend the hall, bestowed auspicious brocade from within the palace, and ordered that all his writings be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He personally recited Ding's poem 《Seeing Off a Guest on the Western River》, summoned him to ascend the hall, bestowed auspicious brocade from within the palace, and ordered that all his writings be submitted.

sentences.zh: 遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，訓、註敗，多誅公卿，中外危惴。

translations.literal: That year, when Xun and Zhu fell, many chief ministers were executed and court and country were gripped by fear.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when Xun and Zhu fell from power, many chief ministers were executed, and court and country alike lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 及改元，天子禦前殿，仇士良請以神策仗衛殿門，定力爭罷之。

translations.literal: When the era name was changed, the Son of Heaven attended the front hall; Qiu Shiliang requested that Shence army halberds guard the palace gates, and Ding forcefully argued until the proposal was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the era name was changed, the Son of Heaven attended the front hall; Qiu Shiliang requested that Shence army halberds guard the palace gates, and Ding argued forcefully until the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又請許左右史從宰相至延英記所言，執政不悅，改太子詹事。

translations.literal: He also requested permitting the Left and Right Historians to follow the chief ministers to Yanying Hall to record their words; the ruling ministers were displeased, and he was transferred to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that the Left and Right Historians be allowed to follow the chief ministers to Yanying Hall to record their words; the ruling ministers were displeased, and he was transferred to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃兼太子太師，上日欲會尚書省，定據禮當集詹事府，詔可。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan concurrently held Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; on a court day he wished to convene at the Secretariat; Ding argued that according to rites they ought to assemble at the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, and the edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan concurrently served as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; on a court day he wished to convene at the Secretariat, but Ding argued that according to rite they ought to assemble at the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, and the edict approved his view.

sentences.zh: 論者多其正。

translations.literal: Many in discussion praised his correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Many commentators praised his correctness.

sentences.zh: 換衛尉卿，以散騎常侍致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of Guardians and retired as Regular Attendant of the Privy Counselors.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commandant of Guardians and retired with the title Regular Attendant of the Privy Counselors.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書，謚曰節。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously made Minister of Works; posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Jie.

sentences.zh: 初，源寂使新羅，其國人傳定《黑水碑》、《畫鶴記》；

translations.literal: At first Yuan Ji was envoy to Silla, and people of that country transmitted Ding's 《Black Water Stele Inscription》 and 《Record of the Painted Crane》;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuan Ji served as envoy to Silla, people of that kingdom circulated Ding's 《Black Water Stele Inscription》 and 《Record of the Painted Crane》;

sentences.zh: 韋休符使西蕃，所館寫定《商山記》於屏。

translations.literal: Wei Xiufu was envoy to the Western Tibetans; at his lodging Ding's 《Record of Mount Shang》 was written on a screen.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xiufu served as envoy to the Western Tibetans, Ding's 《Record of Mount Shang》 was copied onto a screen at his lodging.

sentences.zh: 其名播戎夷如此。

translations.literal: His reputation spread among the frontier peoples to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread among the frontier peoples to such a degree.

sentences.zh: 審，字退思。

translations.literal: Shen, courtesy name Tuisi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, whose courtesy name was Tuisi.

sentences.zh: 開成中，為諫議大夫，拜桂管觀察使，歷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: During Kaicheng he served as Remonstrance Censor, was appointed Military Commissioner of Guiguan, and served as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaicheng era he served as Remonstrance Censor, was appointed Military Commissioner of Guiguan, and later served as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 監有孔子碑，武後所立，睿宗署額。

translations.literal: The Directorate had a stele to Confucius, erected by Empress Wu, with an inscription by Emperor Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate held a stele to Confucius, erected by Empress Wu, with an inscription penned by Emperor Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 審請琢「周」著「唐」。

translations.literal: Shen requested that "Zhou" be carved out and "Tang" added.
translations.idiomatic: Shen requested that the character "Zhou" be carved away and "Tang" inscribed in its place.

sentences.zh: 終秘書監。

translations.literal: He ended as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子緘，字宗之。

translations.literal: His son Jian, courtesy name Zongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian, whose courtesy name was Zongzhi.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，歷京兆、河南尹。

translations.literal: At the start of Qianfu he successively served as prefect of the Capital District and prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianfu era he successively served as prefect of the Capital District and prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 李虞仲，字見之。

translations.literal: Li Yuzhong, courtesy name Jianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuzhong, whose courtesy name was Jianzhi.

sentences.zh: 父端，附見《文藝傳》。

translations.literal: His father Duan is treated in the 《Treatise on Literature and Art》.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duan is discussed in the 《Treatise on Literature and Art》.

sentences.zh: 虞仲第進士、宏辭，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Yuzhong passed the jinshi and the prestigious composition examinations and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhong passed the jinshi examination and the prestigious composition examination, and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 建言：「謚者，所以表德懲惡，《春秋》褒貶法也。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Posthumous titles exist to display virtue and punish vice; they are the method of praise and blame in the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Posthumous titles exist to display virtue and punish vice; they follow the method of praise and blame in the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.

sentences.zh: 茆土爵祿，僇辱流放，皆緣一時，非以明示百代，然而後之所以知其行者，惟謚是觀。

translations.literal: Grants of fief and salary, disgrace and exile—all are matters of the moment, not intended for open display across a hundred generations; yet how later ages come to know a man's conduct depends on viewing his posthumous title alone.
translations.idiomatic: Grants of fief and salary, disgrace and exile—all are matters of the moment, not meant for open display across a hundred generations; yet how later ages learn what a man did depends on his posthumous title alone.

sentences.zh: 古者將葬請謚，今近或二三年，遠乃數十年，然後請謚。

translations.literal: In antiquity posthumous titles were requested as burial approached; today in near cases it may be two or three years, in distant cases several decades, before they are requested.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity posthumous titles were requested as burial approached; today, in some cases two or three years pass, in others several decades, before a title is requested.

sentences.zh: 人歿已久，風績湮歇，采諸傳聞，不可考信，誄狀雖在，言與事浮。

translations.literal: The person has been dead for a long time; reputation and achievements are lost; what is gathered from hearsay cannot be verified, and though the eulogy and petition remain, the words float free of the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The person has long been dead, reputation and achievements have faded, what is gathered from hearsay cannot be verified, and though the eulogy and petition remain, the words no longer match the facts.

sentences.zh: 臣請凡得謚者，前葬一月，請考功刺太常定議，其不請與請而過時者，聽御史劾舉。

translations.literal: I request that for all granted posthumous titles, one month before burial the Directorate of Personnel send notice to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to fix the proposal; for those who do not request or who request after the deadline, let the censorate impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: I request that for all who receive posthumous titles, one month before burial the Directorate of Personnel notify the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to settle the proposal; for those who fail to request or who request after the deadline, let the censorate impeach them.

sentences.zh: 居京師不得過半期，居外一期。

translations.literal: In the capital the period may not exceed half a year; outside the capital, one year.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the deadline may not exceed half a year; outside the capital, one year.

sentences.zh: 若善惡著而不請，許考功察行謚之。

translations.literal: If good or evil is well established and no request is made, let the Directorate of Personnel investigate conduct and bestow a title.
translations.idiomatic: If good or evil is already well established and no request is made, let the Directorate of Personnel investigate conduct and bestow a title.

sentences.zh: 節行卓異，雖無官及官卑者，在所以聞。」

translations.literal: For exceptional integrity and conduct, even for those without office or of low rank, let the locality where word is heard report it."
translations.idiomatic: For exceptional integrity and conduct, even for those without office or of low rank, let the locality where they are known report it."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，以兵部郎中知制誥，進中書舍人，出為華州刺史，歷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Baoli, as Bureau Director in the Ministry of War he concurrently drafted imperial edicts; he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, went out as prefect of Huazhou, and served as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli era, as Bureau Director in the Ministry of War he concurrently drafted imperial edicts; he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, sent out as prefect of Huazhou, and later served as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 簡儉寡欲，時望歸重。

translations.literal: Plain and frugal, with few desires, he commanded the esteem of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and frugal, with few desires, he commanded the respect of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-five; was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five and was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 李翺，字習之，後魏尚書左僕射沖十世孫。

translations.literal: Li Ao, courtesy name Xizhi, was tenth-generation descendant of Chong, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ao, whose courtesy name was Xizhi, was tenth-generation descendant of Chong, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，始調校書郎，累遷。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi, was first appointed Collator, and was repeatedly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was first appointed Collator, and was repeatedly promoted.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為國子博士、史館脩撰。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanhe era he served as Erudite of the Directorate of Education and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe era he served as Erudite of the Directorate of Education and as a compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 常謂史官紀事不得實，乃建言：「大氐人之行，非大善大惡暴於世者，皆訪於人。

translations.literal: He often said that historians did not record events truthfully, and submitted a memorial: "For the most part men's conduct, unless great good or great evil that blazes before the world, is gathered by asking people.
translations.idiomatic: He often said that historians did not record events truthfully, and submitted a memorial: "For the most part men's conduct, unless great good or great evil that blazes before the world, is gathered by asking others.

sentences.zh: 人不周知，故取行狀謚牒。

translations.literal: People do not know everything, so petitions of conduct and posthumous-title memorials are relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: People do not know everything, so historians rely on petitions of conduct and posthumous-title memorials.

sentences.zh: 然其為狀者，皆故吏門生，茍言虛美，溺於文而忘其理。

translations.literal: Yet those who write such petitions are all former subordinates and disciples; they speak empty praise, drowning in words and forgetting the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who write such petitions are all former subordinates and disciples; they speak empty praise, drowning in words and forgetting the truth.

sentences.zh: 臣請指事載功，則賢不肖易見。

translations.literal: I request that specific deeds and achievements be recorded, then the worthy and unworthy will be easy to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: I request that specific deeds and achievements be recorded, so that the worthy and unworthy will be easy to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 如言魏徵，但記其諫爭語，足以為直言；

translations.literal: For example, in speaking of Wei Zheng, record only his remonstrances and disputations—enough to show forthright speech;
translations.idiomatic: For example, in speaking of Wei Zheng, record only his remonstrances and disputations—enough to show forthright speech;

sentences.zh: 段秀實，但記倒用司農印追逆兵，笏擊朱泚，足以為忠烈。

translations.literal: Duan Xiushi, record only his misuse of the Minister of Granaries seal to recall mutinous troops and his tablet-strike against Zhu Ci—enough to show loyal martyrdom.
