translations.idiomatic: For Duan Xiushi, record only his misuse of the Minister of Granaries seal to recall mutinous troops and his tablet-strike against Zhu Ci—enough to show loyal martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 不者，願敕考功、太常、史館勿受。

translations.literal: Otherwise, I ask that the Directorate of Personnel, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Historiography Institute be ordered not to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I ask that the Directorate of Personnel, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Historiography Institute be ordered not to accept such petitions.

sentences.zh: 如此可以傳信後世矣。」

translations.literal: In this way trust may be transmitted to later ages."
translations.idiomatic: In this way what is recorded may be trusted by later ages."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又條興復太平大略曰：

translations.literal: He also set forth a general outline for restoring peace:
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth a general outline for restoring great peace:

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，懷不廷臣，誅畔賊，刷五聖憤恥，自古中興之盛無以加。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession you have cherished unruly ministers, executed rebellious bandits, and wiped clean the shame and rage of the Five Sagely Emperors; no restoration since antiquity has surpassed this splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession you have cherished ministers who would not submit, executed rebellious bandits, and wiped clean the shame and rage of the Five Sagely Emperors; no restoration since antiquity has surpassed this splendor.

sentences.zh: 臣見聖德所不可及者，若淄青生口夏侯澄等四十七人，為賊逼脅，質其父母妻子而驅之戰，陛下俘之，赦不誅，詔田弘正隨材授職，欲歸者縱之。

translations.literal: I see in Your Majesty's unattainable sacred virtue such cases as the forty-seven captives from Ziqing, including Xia Houcheng, forced by rebels, with parents, wives, and children held as hostages and driven into battle; Your Majesty captured them yet pardoned without execution, ordering Tian Hongzheng to assign posts according to capacity, and releasing those who wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: I see in Your Majesty's incomparable sacred virtue such cases as the forty-seven captives from Ziqing, including Xia Houcheng, who were forced by rebels to fight with their parents, wives, and children held as hostages; Your Majesty captured them yet pardoned them without execution, ordered Tian Hongzheng to assign posts according to their abilities, and released those who wished to return home.

sentences.zh: 澄等得生歸，轉以相謂，賊眾莫不懷盛德，無肯拒戰。

translations.literal: Chen and the others returned alive and told one another of it; among the rebel host none failed to harbor Your Majesty's grand virtue, and none would fight in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and the others returned alive and spread word among themselves; among the rebel host none failed to cherish Your Majesty's grand virtue, and none would fight in resistance.

sentences.zh: 劉悟所以能一昔斬師道者，以三軍皆苦賊而匿就陛下，故不淹日成大功。

translations.literal: The reason Liu Wu was able in one night to behead Shi Daodao was that the whole army hated the rebels and secretly inclined toward Your Majesty, so without delay he achieved great success.
translations.idiomatic: The reason Liu Wu was able in a single night to behead Shi Daodao was that the whole army hated the rebels and secretly inclined toward Your Majesty, so in no time he achieved great success.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: First point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first point.

sentences.zh: 今歲關中麥不收，陛下哀民之窮，下明詔蠲賦十萬石，群臣動色，百姓歌樂遍畎每。

translations.literal: This year the wheat harvest in Guanzhong failed; Your Majesty pitied the people's destitution and issued a clear edict remitting one hundred thousand shi of taxes; the ministers were moved to tears, and songs of joy spread through every field path.
translations.idiomatic: This year the wheat harvest in Guanzhong failed; Your Majesty pitied the people's destitution and issued a clear edict remitting one hundred thousand shi of taxes; the ministers were moved to tears, and songs of joy spread through every field and lane.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: Second point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second point.

sentences.zh: 昔齊遺魯以女樂，季桓子受之，君臣共觀，三日不朝，孔子行。

translations.literal: Formerly Qi sent female musicians to Lu; Ji Huanzi accepted them, ruler and ministers watched together, and for three days they did not attend court; Confucius departed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Qi sent female musicians to Lu; Ji Huanzi accepted them, ruler and ministers watched together, and for three days they did not attend court, whereupon Confucius departed.

sentences.zh: 今韓弘獻女樂，陛下不受，遂以歸之。

translations.literal: Now Han Hong presented female musicians; Your Majesty did not accept them and had them returned.
translations.idiomatic: Now Han Hong presented female musicians; Your Majesty did not accept them and had them sent back.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: Third point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third point.

sentences.zh: 又出李宗奭妻女於掖廷，以田宅賜沈遵師，聖明寬恕，億兆欣感。

translations.literal: You also released Li Zongshi's wife and daughters from the inner palace quarters and bestowed fields and dwellings on Shen Zunshi—sacred wisdom and clemency, and the myriad people rejoiced in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: You also released Li Zongshi's wife and daughters from the inner palace quarters and bestowed fields and dwellings on Shen Zunshi—sacred wisdom and clemency at which the myriad people rejoiced in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不能盡識。

translations.literal: This subject's dullness cannot comprehend it all.
translations.idiomatic: This subject's dullness cannot comprehend it all.

sentences.zh: 若它詔令一皆類此，武德、貞觀不難及，太平可覆掌而致。

translations.literal: If every other edict were of this kind, Wude and Zhenguan would not be hard to match, and great peace could be attained as easily as turning one's palm.
translations.idiomatic: If every other edict were of this kind, the eras of Wude and Zhenguan would not be hard to match, and great peace could be attained as easily as turning one's palm.

sentences.zh: 臣聞定禍亂者，武功也；

translations.literal: I have heard that settling calamity and disorder is military achievement;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that settling calamity and disorder is a matter of military achievement;

sentences.zh: 復制度、興太平者，文德也。

translations.literal: Restoring institutions and raising great peace is civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring institutions and raising great peace is a matter of civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 今陛下既以武功定海內，若遂革弊事，復高祖、太宗舊制：用忠正而不疑；

translations.literal: Now that Your Majesty has settled the realm by military achievement, if you would at once reform corrupt practices and restore the old systems of Gaozu and Taizong: employ the loyal and upright without doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has settled the realm by military achievement, if you would at once reform corrupt practices and restore the old systems of Gaozu and Taizong—employ the loyal and upright without doubt;

sentences.zh: 屏邪佞而不邇；

translations.literal: Keep the wicked and flattering at a distance;
translations.idiomatic: Keep the wicked and flattering at a distance;

sentences.zh: 改稅法，不督錢而納布帛；

translations.literal: Change the tax law, not pressing for cash but collecting cloth and silk;
translations.idiomatic: Change the tax law, not pressing for cash but collecting cloth and silk;

sentences.zh: 絕進獻，寬百姓租賦；

translations.literal: Cut off tribute offerings, lighten the people's land tax and levies;
translations.idiomatic: Cut off tribute offerings and lighten the people's land tax and levies;

sentences.zh: 厚邊兵，以制蕃戎侵盜；

translations.literal: Strengthen frontier troops to restrain barbarian raids;
translations.idiomatic: Strengthen frontier troops to restrain barbarian raids;

sentences.zh: 數引見待制官，問以時事，通壅蔽之路。

translations.literal: Frequently summon officials awaiting imperial audience, question them on current affairs, and open the path blocked by obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Frequently summon officials awaiting imperial audience, question them on current affairs, and open the path blocked by obstruction.

sentences.zh: 此六者，政之根本，太平所以興。

translations.literal: These six are the roots of government, by which great peace is raised.
translations.idiomatic: These six are the roots of government, by which great peace is raised.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已能行其難，若何而不為其易者乎？

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty has already been able to do what is difficult, why not do what is easy?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty has already been able to do what is difficult, why not do what is easy?

sentences.zh: 以陛下資上聖，如不惑近習容悅之辭，任骨鯁正直，與之脩復故事，以興大化，可不勞而成也。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's endowment of supreme sagehood, if you are not misled by the flattery of near attendants, employ blunt and upright men, work with them to restore former practice and raise great transformation—it may be achieved without labor.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's endowment of supreme sagehood, if you are not misled by the flattery of near attendants, employ blunt and upright men, work with them to restore former practice and raise great transformation, it may be achieved without labor.

sentences.zh: 若一日不事，臣恐大功之後，逸樂易生，進言者必曰：「天下既平矣，陛下可以高枕自安逸。」

translations.literal: If for a single day you do not attend to affairs, I fear that after great success, ease and pleasure will easily arise, and those who speak up will surely say: "The realm is already at peace; Your Majesty may rest high on your pillow in ease and comfort."
translations.idiomatic: If for a single day you do not attend to affairs, I fear that after great success, ease and pleasure will easily arise, and those who speak up will surely say, "The realm is already at peace; Your Majesty may rest high on your pillow in ease and comfort."

sentences.zh: 如是，則高祖、太宗之制度不可以復；

translations.literal: If so, the institutions of Gaozu and Taizong cannot be restored;
translations.idiomatic: If so, the institutions of Gaozu and Taizong cannot be restored;

sentences.zh: 制度不復，則太平未可以至。

translations.literal: If institutions are not restored, great peace cannot arrive.
translations.idiomatic: If institutions are not restored, great peace cannot be attained.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惜陛下當可興之時，而謙讓未為也。

translations.literal: I privately grieve that Your Majesty, at a time when restoration is possible, yet holds back from acting.
translations.idiomatic: I privately grieve that Your Majesty, at a time when restoration is possible, yet holds back from acting.

sentences.zh: 再遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: After two promotions he became Vice Director of the Directorate of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After two promotions he became Vice Director of the Directorate of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 初，諫議大夫李景儉表翺自代。

translations.literal: At first Remonstrance Censor Li Jingjian memorialized that Ao should replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Remonstrance Censor Li Jingjian memorialized that Ao should replace him.

sentences.zh: 景儉斥，翺下除朗州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingjian was dismissed; Ao was demoted and appointed prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian was dismissed, and Ao was demoted and appointed prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為禮部郎中。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was summoned as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was summoned to serve as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 翺性峭鯁，論議無所屈，仕不得顯官，怫郁無所發，見宰相李逢吉，面斥其過失，逢吉詭不校，翺恚懼，即移病。

translations.literal: Ao's temperament was sharp and unyielding; in debate he yielded to no one. In office he never attained prominent posts; frustrated with nowhere to vent, he saw Chief Minister Li Fengji and rebuked his faults to his face. Fengji feigned not to take offense; Ao, enraged and afraid, immediately submitted a sickness resignation.
translations.idiomatic: Ao's temperament was sharp and unyielding; in debate he yielded to no one. In office he never attained prominent posts, and frustrated with nowhere to vent, he went to see Chief Minister Li Fengji and rebuked his faults to his face. Fengji feigned not to take offense; Ao, enraged and afraid, immediately submitted a sickness resignation.

sentences.zh: 滿百日，有司白免官，逢吉更表為廬州刺史。

translations.literal: After the hundred days were complete, the appropriate office reported dismissal from office; Fengji further memorialized to appoint him prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the hundred days were complete, the appropriate office reported that he should be dismissed from office; Fengji further memorialized to appoint him prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 時州旱，遂疫，逋捐系路，亡籍口四萬，權豪賤市田屋牟厚利，而窶戶仍輸賦。

translations.literal: At the time the prefecture suffered drought, then pestilence; tax defaulters clogged the roads; forty thousand persons were lost from the registers; powerful families bought fields and houses cheaply for thick profit, while impoverished households still paid taxes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the prefecture suffered drought and then pestilence; tax defaulters clogged the roads, forty thousand persons were lost from the registers, powerful families bought fields and houses cheaply for thick profit, while impoverished households still paid taxes.

sentences.zh: 翺下教使以田占租，無得隱，收豪室稅萬二千緡，貧弱以安。

translations.literal: Ao issued an instruction that rent be assessed by land held, with no concealment permitted; he collected twelve thousand strings from great houses, and the poor were given relief.
translations.idiomatic: Ao issued an instruction that rent be assessed by land held, with no concealment permitted; he collected twelve thousand strings from great houses, and the poor were given relief.

sentences.zh: 入為諫議大夫，知制誥，改中書舍人。

translations.literal: He entered court as Remonstrance Censor, concurrently drafting imperial edicts, and was changed to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Remonstrance Censor with concurrent charge of drafting imperial edicts, and was then made Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 柏耆使滄州，翺盛言其才。

translations.literal: Bo Qi was envoy to Cangzhou; Ao greatly praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo Qi served as envoy to Cangzhou, Ao greatly praised his talent.

sentences.zh: 耆得罪，由是左遷少府少監。

translations.literal: When Qi fell from favor, Ao was demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell from favor, Ao was demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 後歷遷桂管湖南觀察使、山南東道節度使，卒。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Military Commissioner of Guiguan and Hunan and Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he successively served as Military Commissioner of Guiguan and Hunan and Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 翺始從昌黎韓愈為文章，辭致渾厚，見推當時，故有司亦謚曰文。

translations.literal: Ao had first studied composition under Han Yu of Changli; his style was rich and full, and he was admired in his day; therefore the authorities also gave him the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Ao had first studied composition under Han Yu of Changli; his style was rich and full, and he was admired in his day; therefore the authorities also gave him the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 盧簡辭，字子策。

translations.literal: Lu Jianci, courtesy name Zice.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jianci, whose courtesy name was Zice.

sentences.zh: 父綸，別傳。

translations.literal: His father Lun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lun has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 與兄簡能、弟弘止、簡求皆有文，並第進士。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Jianneng and younger brothers Hongzhi and Jianqiu, all were accomplished in letters and together passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He, his elder brother Jianneng, and his younger brothers Hongzhi and Jianqiu were all accomplished in letters and together passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷佐帥府，入遷侍御史，習知法令及臺閣舊事。

translations.literal: He served successively on commanders' staffs, entered court as Attending Censor, and was versed in statutes and old precedents of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively on commanders' staffs, entered court as Attending Censor, and was versed in statutes and old precedents of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，黎幹子煟詣臺請復葉縣故田，有司莫能知，簡辭獨詰曰：「按幹坐黨魚朝恩誅，貲田皆沒，大歷後數十年，比有赦令，無原洗之言，煟安得冒論？」

translations.literal: During Baoli, Wei, son of Li Gan, came to the censorate requesting restoration of former fields in Ye County; no office could decide the matter. Jianci alone questioned: "According to the record, Gan was executed for associating with Yu Chaoen; his property and fields were all confiscated. For decades after the Dali era, whenever there were amnesties, none contained language of restoration; how can Wei presumptuously argue?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli era, Wei, son of Li Gan, came to the censorate requesting restoration of former fields in Ye County; no office could decide the matter. Jianci alone questioned: "According to the record, Gan was executed for associating with Yu Chaoen; his property and fields were all confiscated. For decades after the Dali era, whenever there were amnesties, none contained language of restoration; how can Wei presumptuously argue?"

sentences.zh: 不為治。

translations.literal: He would not handle it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to handle the case.

sentences.zh: 福建鹽鐵院官盧昂坐贓，簡辭窮按，乃得金床、瑟瑟枕大如鬥。

translations.literal: The Fujian Salt and Iron Commission official Lu Ang was charged with corruption; Jianci investigated thoroughly and recovered a golden bed and a sese pillow as large as a bushel.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian Salt and Iron Commission official Lu Ang was charged with corruption; Jianci investigated thoroughly and recovered a golden bed and a sese pillow as large as a bushel measure.

sentences.zh: 敬宗曰：「禁中無此，昂為吏可知矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong said: "Nothing like this exists within the palace; Ang's conduct as an official can be imagined."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong said, "Nothing like this exists within the palace; Ang's conduct as an official can be imagined."

sentences.zh: 李程鎮太原，表為節度判官。

translations.literal: When Li Cheng governed Taiyuan, he recommended Jianci as military commission assessor.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cheng governed Taiyuan, he recommended Jianci as military commission assessor.

sentences.zh: 入授考功員外郎，累擢湖南、浙西觀察使，以檢校工部尚書為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Directorate of Personnel, was repeatedly promoted to Military Commissioner of Hunan and Zhexi, and as Acting Minister of Works served as Military Commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Director of the Directorate of Personnel, was repeatedly promoted to Military Commissioner of Hunan and Zhexi, and as Acting Minister of Works served as Military Commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 徙山南東道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐事貶衢州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to prefect of Quzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to prefect of Quzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 簡能，見《鄭註傳》。

translations.literal: Jianneng is treated in the biography of Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Jianneng is discussed in the biography of Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 其子知猷，字子謨，中進士第，登宏辭，補秘書省正字。

translations.literal: His son Zhiyou, courtesy name Zimo, passed the jinshi, passed the prestigious composition examination, and was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiyou, whose courtesy name was Zimo, passed the jinshi examination and the prestigious composition examination, and was appointed Proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 蕭鄴鎮荊南、劍南，再辟掌書記。

translations.literal: When Xiao Ye governed Jingnan and Jiannan, he twice recruited Zhiyou as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Ye governed Jingnan and Jiannan, he twice recruited Zhiyou as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 入遷右補闕，出為饒州刺史，以政最聞。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Remonstrance Officer, went out as prefect of Raozhou, and was renowned for outstanding governance.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Right Remonstrance Officer, was sent out as prefect of Raozhou, and was renowned for outstanding governance.

sentences.zh: 累進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted until he reached Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 朱玫亂，避難不出。

translations.literal: During Zhu Mei's rebellion, he took refuge and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Mei's rebellion, he took refuge and did not emerge from seclusion.

sentences.zh: 僖宗還京，召拜工部侍郎、史館脩撰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works and Drafting Compiler in the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital, Zhiyou was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works and Drafting Compiler in the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 歷太常卿、戶部尚書，至太子太師。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Minister of Revenue, reaching Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Minister of Revenue, eventually rising to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 昭宗為劉季述所幽，感憤卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was imprisoned by Liu Jishu, he died of anger and indignation; was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong was imprisoned by Liu Jishu, Zhiyou died of anger and indignation and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 知猷器量渾厚，世推為長者。

translations.literal: Zhiyou's capacity and bearing were generous and steady; the age acclaimed him as an elder worthy of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyou's capacity and bearing were generous and steady, and his contemporaries acclaimed him as a man of elder virtue.

sentences.zh: 善書，有楷法。

translations.literal: He was skilled at calligraphy and had a model in regular script.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at calligraphy and had a distinguished hand in regular script.

sentences.zh: 文辭贍麗。

translations.literal: His literary style was rich and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: His literary style was rich and elegant.

sentences.zh: 子文度，亦貴顯。

translations.literal: His son Wendu also achieved rank and eminence.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wendu also rose to rank and eminence.

sentences.zh: 弘止，字子強，佐劉悟府，累擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Hongzhi, courtesy name Ziqiang, assisted in Liu Wu's headquarters and was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi, whose courtesy name was Ziqiang, served on Liu Wu's staff and was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 沈傳師表為江西團練副使。

translations.literal: Shen Chuanshi recommended him as Deputy Military Training Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chuanshi recommended him for appointment as Deputy Military Training Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 入拜侍御史。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court and was appointed Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 華州刺史宇文鼎、戶部員外盧允中坐贓，詔弘止按訊。

translations.literal: The prefect of Hua Prefecture, Yuwen Ding, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Lu Yunzhong were convicted of embezzlement; Hongzhi was ordered to investigate and examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ding, prefect of Hua Prefecture, and Lu Yunzhong, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, were convicted of embezzlement, and Hongzhi was ordered to investigate and examine the case.

sentences.zh: 文宗將殺鼎，弘止執據罪由允中，鼎乃連坐，不應死，帝釋之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong was about to execute Ding; Hongzhi steadfastly maintained that the guilt lay with Yunzhong, and Ding was implicated only by association and did not deserve death; the emperor released him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was about to execute Ding, but Hongzhi steadfastly maintained that the guilt lay with Yunzhong; Ding had been implicated only by association and did not deserve death, and the emperor released him.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted until he reached Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，詔河北三節度討劉稹。

translations.literal: During Huichang an edict ordered the three military commissioners of Hebei to attack Liu Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era an edict ordered the three military commissioners of Hebei to campaign against Liu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 何弘敬、王元逵先取邢、洺、磁三州，宰相李德裕畏諸帥有請地者，乃以弘止為三州團練觀察留後。

translations.literal: He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui first captured the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci; Chief Minister Li Deyu feared that the commanders would request territories, so Hongzhi was made Acting Military Training and Observation Commissioner of the three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui first captured the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci; Chief Minister Li Deyu feared that the commanders would request territories, so Hongzhi was appointed Acting Military Training and Observation Commissioner of the three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 制未下，稹平，即詔為三州及河北兩鎮宣慰使。

translations.literal: Before the appointment decree was issued Liu Zhen had been suppressed, and Hongzhi was immediately made Pacification Commissioner for the three prefectures and the two Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment decree was issued Liu Zhen had already been suppressed, and Hongzhi was immediately made Pacification Commissioner for the three prefectures and the two Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 還，拜工部侍郎，以戶部領度支。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Works and concurrently charged with the Salt and Grain Commission through the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Works and given concurrent charge of the Salt and Grain Commission through the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，兩池鹽法弊，得費不相償，弘止使判官司空輿檢鉤厘正，條上新法，即表輿兩池使，自是課入歲倍，用度賴之。

translations.literal: At first the salt law of the two pools was corrupt, and revenue did not cover expenses; Hongzhi had his deputy Sikong Yu investigate and rectify matters, submitted a new law in detail, and recommended Yu as Commissioner of the Two Salt Pools; from then on revenue doubled annually, and government expenses depended on it.
translations.idiomatic: At first the salt law governing the two pools was corrupt, and revenue no longer covered expenses; Hongzhi had his deputy Sikong Yu investigate and rectify matters, submitted a detailed new law, and recommended Yu as Commissioner of the Two Salt Pools; from then on annual revenue doubled, and government expenses came to depend on it.

sentences.zh: 逾年，出為武寧節度使。

translations.literal: After a year he went out as Military Commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was sent out as Military Commissioner of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 徐自王智興後，吏卒驕沓，銀刀軍尤不法，弘止戮其尤無狀者，終弘止治，不敢嘩。

translations.literal: Since Wang Zhixing, the officials and soldiers of Xuzhou had grown arrogant and unruly, and the Silver Sabre Army especially violated the law; Hongzhi executed the worst offenders, and throughout his administration they did not dare make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Zhixing's time the officials and soldiers of Xuzhou had grown arrogant and unruly, and the Silver Sabre Army in particular violated the law with impunity; Hongzhi executed the worst offenders, and throughout his administration they did not dare cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒勞。

translations.literal: An especially gracious edict praised and rewarded his labors.
translations.idiomatic: An especially gracious edict praised and rewarded his labors.

sentences.zh: 弘止羸病，丐身還東都，不許。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was frail and ill; he requested leave to return to the Eastern Capital, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was frail and ill; he requested leave to return to the Eastern Capital, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 徙宣武，卒於鎮，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xuanwu and died in office; was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xuanwu and died in office; he was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子虔灌，有美才，終秘書監。

translations.literal: His son Qianguan had outstanding talent and ended as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianguan had outstanding talent and ended his career as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 簡求，字子臧，始從江西王仲舒幕府，兩為裴度、元稹所辟，又佐牛僧孺鎮襄陽，入遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: Jianqiu, courtesy name Zizang, first joined the staff of Wang Zhongshu in Jiangxi, was twice recruited by Pei Du and Yuan Zhen, later assisted Niu Sengru when he governed Xiangyang, and entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiu, whose courtesy name was Zizang, first served on the staff of Wang Zhongshu in Jiangxi, was twice recruited by Pei Du and Yuan Zhen, later assisted Niu Sengru when he governed Xiangyang, and entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，討劉稹，以忠武節度使李彥佐為招討使，各選簡求副之，俾知後務。

translations.literal: During Huichang, in the campaign against Liu Zhen, Li Yanzhuo, Military Commissioner of Zhongwu, was made Pacification Commissioner; each chose Jianqiu as his deputy and put him in charge of rear operations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era, in the campaign against Liu Zhen, Li Yanzhuo, Military Commissioner of Zhongwu, was made Pacification Commissioner; each commander chose Jianqiu as his deputy and put him in charge of rear operations.

sentences.zh: 歷蘇、壽二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Su and Shou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as prefect of Su and Shou prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大中九年，党項擾邊，拜涇原渭武節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong the Tangut people harassed the frontier; he was appointed Military Commissioner of Jingyuan, Wei, and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dazhong, when the Tangut people harassed the frontier, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Jingyuan, Wei, and Wu.

sentences.zh: 徙義武、鳳翔、河東三鎮。

translations.literal: He was transferred among the three circuits of Yiwu, Fengxiang, and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred among the three circuits of Yiwu, Fengxiang, and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 簡求為政長權變，文不害，居邊善綏禦，人皆安之。

translations.literal: Jianqiu governed with flexible authority, without harming through bureaucratic formalism; on the frontier he was skilled at pacifying and defending, and the people all felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiu governed with flexible authority and without letting bureaucratic formalism do harm; on the frontier he was skilled at pacifying and defending, and the people all felt secure.

sentences.zh: 太原統退渾、契、沙陀三部，難馴制，它帥或與詛盟，質子弟，然寇掠不為止。

translations.literal: At Taiyuan he oversaw the Tuihun, Qi, and Shatuo tribes; they were hard to control and tame; other commanders sometimes made sworn covenants with them and held their sons as hostages, yet raiding did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan he had jurisdiction over the Tuihun, Qi, and Shatuo tribes, who were hard to control; other commanders sometimes made sworn covenants with them and held their sons as hostages, yet raiding did not cease.

sentences.zh: 簡求歸所質，開示至誠，虜憚其恩信，不敢亂。

translations.literal: Jianqiu returned the hostages, displayed utmost sincerity, and the barbarians feared his grace and trustworthiness and did not dare cause disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiu returned the hostages, displayed the utmost sincerity, and the frontier peoples, awed by his grace and trustworthiness, did not dare cause disorder.

sentences.zh: 久之，辭疾，以太子少師致仕，還東都，治園沼林苑，與賓客置酒自娛。

translations.literal: After a long time he pleaded illness, retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, returned to the Eastern Capital, tended gardens, ponds, and groves, and entertained guests with wine for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he pleaded illness, retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, returned to the Eastern Capital, tended gardens, ponds, and groves, and entertained guests with wine for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-six; was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-six and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子嗣業、汝弼，皆中進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Siye and Rubi both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Siye and Rubi both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 汝弼以祠部員外郎知制誥，從昭宗遷洛。

translations.literal: Rubi, as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites drafting imperial edicts, followed Emperor Zhaozong in the move to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi, serving as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites with charge of drafting imperial edicts, followed Emperor Zhaozong in the move to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 方柳璨斫喪王室，汝弼懼，移疾去，客上黨。

translations.literal: Just as Liu Can was ravaging the royal house, Rubi grew fearful, pleaded illness and departed, and took refuge in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Liu Can was ravaging the royal house, Rubi grew fearful, pleaded illness and departed, and took refuge in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 後依李克用，克用表為節度副使。

translations.literal: Later he attached himself to Li Keyong, who memorialized to appoint him as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attached himself to Li Keyong, who memorialized to appoint him deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太原府子亭，簡求所署多在，每宴亭中，未嘗居賓位，西向俯首，人美其有禮。

translations.literal: At Ziting in the Taiyuan prefectural compound, many inscriptions by Jianqiu still remained; whenever Rubi banqueted there he never took the guest seat, but faced west and bowed his head; people praised his propriety.
translations.idiomatic: At Ziting in the Taiyuan prefectural compound, many inscriptions by Jianqiu still remained; whenever Rubi banqueted there he never took the guest seat but faced west and bowed his head, and people praised his propriety.

sentences.zh: 嗣業子文紀，後貴顯。

translations.literal: Siye's son Wenji later achieved rank and eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Siye's son Wenji later rose to rank and eminence.

sentences.zh: 高元裕，字景圭，其先蓋渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Yuanyu, courtesy name Jinggui, his ancestors were probably people of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanyu, whose courtesy name was Jinggui, was probably descended from people of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累辟節度府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以右補闕召，道商州，會方士趙歸真擅乘驛馬，元裕詆曰：「天子置驛，爾敢疾驅邪？」

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Remonstrance Officer, on the road through Shang Prefecture he encountered the Taoist adept Zhao Guizhen riding post horses without authorization; Yuanyu denounced him, saying: "The Son of Heaven established the post stations — how dare you drive at full speed?"
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Right Remonstrance Officer, on the road through Shang Prefecture he encountered the Taoist adept Zhao Guizhen riding post horses without authorization; Yuanyu denounced him, saying, "The Son of Heaven established the post stations — how dare you drive at full speed?"

sentences.zh: 命左右奪之，還，具以聞。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to seize the horse; on returning he reported the matter in full.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to seize the horse; on returning he reported the matter in full.

sentences.zh: 敬宗視朝不時，稍稍決事禁中，宦豎恣放，大臣不得進見。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong held court irregularly, gradually deciding affairs within the palace; eunuchs ran wild, and chief ministers could not gain audience.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong held court irregularly and gradually decided affairs within the palace; eunuchs ran wild, and chief ministers could not gain audience.

sentences.zh: 元裕諫曰：「今西頭勢乃重南衙，樞密之權過宰相。」

translations.literal: Yuanyu remonstrated: "Today the western offices weigh heavier than the southern court, and the Privy Commissioner wields greater power than the chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu remonstrated: "Today the western offices weigh heavier than the southern court, and the Privy Commissioner wields greater power than the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 帝頗寤而不能有所檢制，人皆危之。

translations.literal: The emperor somewhat awoke to this but could not impose any restraint; everyone felt alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor somewhat awoke to this but could not impose any restraint, and everyone felt alarm.

sentences.zh: 俄換侍御史內供奉，士始相賀。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attending Censor with Internal Attendance; scholars at last began to congratulate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Attending Censor with Internal Attendance, and scholars at last began to congratulate one another.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔高其節，擢諫議大夫，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin esteemed his integrity and promoted him to Remonstrance Censor, then to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin esteemed his integrity and promoted him to Remonstrance Censor, then to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 鄭註入翰林，元裕當書命，乃言「以醫術侍」，註愧憾。

translations.literal: When Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin Academy, Yuanyu was to draft the appointment and wrote "serving with medical arts"; Zhu was shamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin Academy, Yuanyu was to draft the appointment and wrote "serving with medical arts"; Zhu was shamed and resentful.

sentences.zh: 及宗閔得罪，元裕坐出餞，貶閬州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin fell from grace, Yuanyu was implicated for seeing him off with a farewell feast and was demoted to prefect of Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin fell from grace, Yuanyu was implicated for seeing him off with a farewell feast and was demoted to prefect of Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 註死，復授諫議大夫、翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: After Zhu died, Yuanyu was again appointed Remonstrance Censor and Hanlin Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu died, Yuanyu was again appointed Remonstrance Censor and Hanlin Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 莊恪太子立，擇可輔導者，乃兼賓客。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhuangke was established, a suitable mentor was chosen, and Yuanyu also served as Crown Prince's Guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhuangke was established, a suitable mentor was chosen, and Yuanyu also served as Crown Prince's Guest.

sentences.zh: 進御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Censor.

sentences.zh: 即建言：「紀綱地官屬須選，有不稱職者，請罷之。」

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial: "Officials in the departments that maintain order must be selected; those not fulfilling their duties should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial: "Officials in the departments that maintain order must be selected, and those not fulfilling their duties should be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 於是監察御史杜宣猷、柳瑰、崔郢、侍御史魏中庸、高弘簡並奪職。

translations.literal: Thereupon Investigating Censors Du Xuanyou, Liu Gui, and Cui Ying, and Attending Censors Wei Zhongyong and Gao Hongjian all had their posts removed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Investigating Censors Du Xuanyou, Liu Gui, and Cui Ying, and Attending Censors Wei Zhongyong and Gao Hongjian all had their posts removed.

sentences.zh: 故事，三司監院官帶御史者，號「外臺」，得察風俗，舉不法。

translations.literal: According to precedent, supervisory officials of the Three Offices who bore the censor title were called "Outer Platform"; they could inspect local customs and report unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: According to precedent, supervisory officials of the Three Offices who bore the censor title were called the "Outer Platform"; they could inspect local customs and report unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 元和中，李夷簡因請按察本道州縣。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era Li Yijian requested to inspect the prefectures and counties of his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era Li Yijian requested permission to inspect the prefectures and counties of his circuit.

sentences.zh: 後益不職。

translations.literal: Later they grew even less effective in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Later they grew even less effective in their duties.

sentences.zh: 元裕請監院御史隸本臺，得專督察。

translations.literal: Yuanyu requested that supervisory censors of the offices be placed under the main censorate so they could conduct dedicated inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu requested that supervisory censors of the offices be placed under the main censorate so they could conduct dedicated inspection.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 累擢尚書左丞，領吏部選。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and oversaw selections in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and oversaw selections in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為宣歙觀察使，入授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He went out as Military Training and Observation Commissioner of Xuancai and entered court again as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Military Training and Observation Commissioner of Xuancai and entered court again as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 拜山南東道節度使，封渤海郡公，奏蠲逋賦甚眾。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai Commandery, and memorialized to remit a great many unpaid taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai Commandery, and memorialized to remit a great many unpaid taxes.

sentences.zh: 在鎮五年，復以吏部尚書召，卒於道，年七十六，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: After five years in office he was again summoned as Minister of Personnel; he died on the road at seventy-six; was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office he was again summoned as Minister of Personnel; he died on the road at seventy-six and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元裕性勤約，通經術，敏於為吏，巖巖有風采，推重於時。

translations.literal: Yuanyu was by nature diligent and frugal, versed in the classics, quick as an official, imposing in bearing, and highly regarded in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu was by nature diligent and frugal, versed in the classics, quick as an official, imposing in bearing, and highly regarded in his time.

sentences.zh: 自侍講為中丞，文宗難其代，元裕表言兄少逸才可任，因以命之，世榮其遷。

translations.literal: From Hanlin lecturer to Chief Censor, Wenzong found his replacement difficult; Yuanyu memorialized that his elder brother Shaoyi was capable of the post, and the appointment was made accordingly; the age honored the transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanyu moved from Hanlin lecturer to Chief Censor, Wenzong found his replacement difficult; Yuanyu memorialized that his elder brother Shaoyi was capable of the post, and the appointment was made accordingly; the age honored the transfer.

sentences.zh: 少逸，長慶末為侍御史，坐失舉劾，貶贊善大夫，累遷諫議大夫，乃代元裕。

translations.literal: Shaoyi, at the end of Changqing, served as Attending Censor; for failure to impeach he was demoted to Senior Adviser and was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Censor, then replaced Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi, at the end of the Changqing era, served as Attending Censor; for failure to impeach he was demoted to Senior Adviser, was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Censor, and then replaced Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 稍進給事中，出為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Supervising Censor and went out as Military Training and Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Supervising Censor and was sent out as Military Training and Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 中人責峽石驛吏供餅惡，鞭之，少逸封餅以聞。

translations.literal: An eunuch blamed the station keeper of Xiashi Post for providing poor cakes and whipped him; Shaoyi sealed the cakes and reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: An eunuch blamed the station keeper of Xiashi Post for providing poor cakes and whipped him; Shaoyi sealed the cakes and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣宗怒，召使者責曰：「山谷間是餅豈易具邪？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong grew angry and summoned the messenger, scolding him: "In a mountain gorge, are such cakes easy to prepare?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong grew angry and summoned the messenger, scolding him: "In a mountain gorge, are such cakes easy to prepare?"

sentences.zh: 謫隸恭陵，中人皆斂手。

translations.literal: He was demoted to labor at Gong Mausoleum, and the eunuchs all held their hands back.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to labor at Gong Mausoleum, and the eunuchs all held their hands back.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired as Minister of War and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Minister of War and died.

sentences.zh: 元裕始名允中，太和中改今名。

translations.literal: Yuanyu was originally named Yunzhong; in the Taihe era his present name was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu was originally named Yunzhong; in the Taihe era he adopted his present name.

sentences.zh: 元裕子璩，字瑩之。

translations.literal: Yuanyu's son Ji, courtesy name Yingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu's son Ji, whose courtesy name was Yingzhi.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累佐使府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly assisted in commissioners' headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served on commissioners' staffs.

sentences.zh: 以左拾遺為翰林學士，擢諫議大夫。

translations.literal: As Left Remembrancer he became Hanlin Academician and was promoted to Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: As Left Remembrancer he became Hanlin Academician and was promoted to Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 近世學士超省郎進官者，惟鄭顥以尚主，而璩以寵升雲。

translations.literal: In recent times among Hanlin scholars elevated above provincial bureau ranks, only Zheng Hao rose by marrying the princess, while Ji rose through favor like clouds ascending.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times among Hanlin scholars elevated above provincial bureau ranks, only Zheng Hao rose by marrying the princess, while Ji rose through imperial favor alone.

sentences.zh: 懿宗時，拜劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yizong's reign he was appointed Military Commissioner of Eastern Chuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yizong's reign he was appointed Military Commissioner of Eastern Chuan in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 召拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Junior Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Junior Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 閱月卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: Within a month he died; was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太常博士曹鄴建言：「璩，宰相，交遊鬼雜，取多蹊徑，謚法『不思妄愛曰刺』，請謚為刺。」

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cao Ye submitted a memorial: "Ji, a chief minister, consorted with disreputable company and took many irregular paths; the posthumous title canon says 'One who loves recklessly without reflection is called Ci (Piercing),' I request the posthumous title Ci."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cao Ye submitted a memorial: "Ji, a chief minister, consorted with disreputable company and took many irregular paths; the posthumous title canon says 'One who loves recklessly without reflection is called Ci (Piercing),' and I request the posthumous title Ci."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was accepted.

sentences.zh: 封敖，字碩夫，其先蓋冀州蓚人。

translations.literal: Feng Ao, courtesy name Shuofu, his ancestors were probably people of Zhu Prefecture in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ao, whose courtesy name was Shuofu, was probably descended from people of Zhu Prefecture in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 元和中，署進士第，江西裴堪辟置其府，轉右拾遺，雅為宰相李德裕所器。

translations.literal: During Yuanhe he placed in the jinshi examination; Pei Kan of Jiangxi recruited him to his staff; he became Right Remembrancer and was greatly valued by Chief Minister Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he placed in the jinshi examination; Pei Kan of Jiangxi recruited him to his staff; he became Right Remembrancer and was greatly valued by Chief Minister Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，以左司員外郎召為翰林學士，三遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he was summoned as Left Secretary and Hanlin Academician, and was thrice promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huichang era he was summoned as Left Secretary and Hanlin Academician, and was thrice promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 敖屬辭贍敏，不為奇澀，語切而理勝。

translations.literal: Ao's writings were rich and nimble, never obscure or harsh; his language was direct and his reasoning prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Ao's writings were rich and nimble, never obscure or harsh; his language was direct and his reasoning prevailed.

sentences.zh: 武宗使作詔書慰邊將傷夷者，曰：「傷居爾體，痛在朕躬。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong had him draft an edict to comfort frontier generals wounded in battle; it read: "The wound is in your body, but the pain is in My own person."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong had him draft an edict to comfort frontier generals wounded in battle; it read, "The wound is in your body, but the pain is in My own person."

sentences.zh: 帝善其如意出，賜以宮錦。

translations.literal: The emperor approved how aptly it came forth and rewarded him with palace brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved how aptly it came forth and rewarded him with palace brocade.

sentences.zh: 劉稹平，德裕以定策功進太尉，時敖草其制曰：「謀皆予同，言不它惑。」

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen was suppressed, Li Deyu for his merit in settling strategy was promoted to Grand Preceptor; at that time Ao drafted the appointment, writing: "In planning we were always of one mind; in speech nothing else misled us."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhen was suppressed, Li Deyu for his merit in settling strategy was promoted to Grand Preceptor; at that time Ao drafted the appointment, writing, "In planning we were always of one mind; in speech nothing else misled us."

sentences.zh: 德裕以能明專任己以成功，謂敖曰：「陸生恨文不迨意，如君此等語，豈易得邪？」

translations.literal: Deyu, able to see clearly that concentrating sole responsibility on himself had brought success, said to Ao: "Master Lu resented when the writing failed to meet his intent; phrases like yours — are they not hard to come by?"
translations.idiomatic: Deyu, seeing clearly that concentrating sole responsibility on himself had brought success, said to Ao, "Master Lu resented when the writing failed to meet his intent; phrases like yours — are they not hard to come by?"

sentences.zh: 解所賜玉帶贈之。

translations.literal: He undid the jade belt he had been given and presented it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He undid the jade belt he had been given and presented it to Ao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜御史中丞，與宰相盧商慮囚，誤縱死罪，復為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Chief Censor; together with Chief Minister Lu Shang he reviewed prisoners and by mistake released men sentenced to death; he was restored to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Chief Censor; together with Chief Minister Lu Shang he reviewed prisoners and by mistake released men sentenced to death, and he was restored to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 大中中，歷平盧、興元節度使。

translations.literal: During Dazhong he successively served as Military Commissioner of Pinglu and Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era he successively served as Military Commissioner of Pinglu and Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，鄭涯開新路，水壞其棧，敖更治斜谷道，行者告便。

translations.literal: At first Zheng Ya opened a new route; floods destroyed its plankways; Ao rebuilt the Xiégu road, and travelers reported it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zheng Ya opened a new route, but floods destroyed its plankways; Ao rebuilt the Xiégu road, and travelers reported it convenient.

sentences.zh: 蓬、果賊依雞山，寇三川，敖遣副使王贄捕平之。

translations.literal: Bandits of Peng and Guo relied on Mount Ji and raided the Three Rivers region; Ao sent his deputy Wang Zan to capture and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits of Peng and Guo relied on Mount Ji and raided the Three Rivers region; Ao sent his deputy Wang Zan to capture and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 加檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Minister of Personnel with check only.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Minister of Personnel with check only.

sentences.zh: 還為太常卿。

translations.literal: On his return he became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 始視事，廷設九部樂，敖宴私第，為御史所劾，徙國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When he first took office he had the Nine Section Music performed in court; Ao banqueted at his private residence and was impeached by the censorate; he was transferred to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took office he had the Nine Section Music performed in court; Ao banqueted at his private residence and was impeached by the censorate, and he was transferred to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 復拜太常，進尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Again appointed Director of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 然少行檢，士但高其才，故不至宰相，卒。

translations.literal: Yet he lacked self-restraint in conduct; scholars only esteemed his talent, so he never reached the chancellorship, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was deficient in personal conduct; scholars admired only his talent, and so he never rose to chancellor. He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子彥卿、望卿，從子特卿，皆第進士。

translations.literal: His sons Yanqing and Wangqing, and his nephew Teqing, all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yanqing and Wangqing, and his nephew Teqing, all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 鄭薰，字子溥，亡鄉里世系。

translations.literal: Zheng Xun, courtesy name Zibo; his native place and family lineage are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xun, whose courtesy name was Zibo, was a man whose native place and family lineage are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷考功郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director in the Bureau of Evaluations and as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director in the Bureau of Evaluations and as a Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 出為宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Observation Commissioner of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Observation Commissioner of Xuan and She.

sentences.zh: 前人不治，薰頗以清力自將。

translations.literal: His predecessors had not governed well; Xun relied greatly on strict integrity to conduct himself.
translations.idiomatic: Previous commissioners had left the region poorly governed, but Xun governed with notable strictness and integrity.

sentences.zh: 牙將素驕，共謀逐出之，薰奔揚州。

translations.literal: The military adjutants had long been arrogant; they plotted together to drive him out, and Xun fled to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison adjutants had long been insubordinate; they conspired to drive him out, and Xun fled to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貶棣王府長史，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Chief Administrator of the Prince of Di's household and assigned as commissioner at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Chief Administrator of the Prince of Di's household and given a nominal post at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 懿宗立，召為太常少卿，擢累吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yizong acceded, Xun was summoned as Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yizong came to the throne, Xun was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was eventually promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時數大赦，階正議光祿大夫者，得蔭一子，門施戟。

translations.literal: At that time there were frequent great amnesties; those whose honorary rank reached Regular Grand Master of Splendid Happiness could benefit one son with office privileges, and halberds were displayed at their gates.
translations.idiomatic: At that time great amnesties were frequent, and those whose honorary rank reached Regular Grand Master of Splendid Happiness were entitled to office privileges for one son and to display halberds at their gates.

sentences.zh: 於是宦人用階請蔭子，薰卻之不肯敘。

translations.literal: Thereupon eunuchs used their honorary ranks to request yin benefits for their sons; Xun refused them and would not register the privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs then used their honorary ranks to request yin privileges for their sons, but Xun turned them away and refused to register the benefits.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜悰才其人，擬判度支，辭；

translations.literal: The chancellor Du Cong recognized his ability and proposed appointing him to head the Bureau of Revenue; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Du Cong, recognizing his talent, proposed appointing him to head the Bureau of Revenue, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 又擬刑部兼御史中丞，固辭，乃免。

translations.literal: He was next proposed for the Ministry of Justice concurrently with Censor in Chief; he firmly declined, and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: He was next proposed for the Ministry of Justice with concurrent appointment as Censor in Chief; he firmly declined, and the appointments were dropped.

sentences.zh: 久之，進左丞。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Left Assistant Minister.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Left Assistant Minister.

sentences.zh: 性愛友，糾族百口，稟不充，求外遷。

translations.literal: By nature he loved his kin; he gathered a clan of more than a hundred mouths, and provisions were insufficient, so he sought transfer outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his kin and supported a clan of more than a hundred people, but his income could not meet their needs, so he sought a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 擬華州刺史，輒留中，為幸侍酬沮。

translations.literal: When he was nominated Governor of Hua Prefecture, the appointment was repeatedly held in the palace and blocked by favored attendants in return for favors.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nominated Governor of Hua Prefecture, the appointment was repeatedly held in abeyance at court and thwarted by favored attendants seeking repayment for favors.

sentences.zh: 後以太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: Later he retired as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired with the title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 薰端勁，再知禮部，舉引寒俊，士類多之。

translations.literal: Xun was upright and firm; twice he oversaw the Ministry of Rites examinations, recommending poor but talented scholars, and the scholar class greatly approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was upright and resolute. Twice he oversaw the Ministry of Rites examinations and promoted poor but talented scholars, winning wide approval among men of letters.

sentences.zh: 既老，號所居為「隱巖」，蒔松於廷，號「七松處士」雲。

translations.literal: When he grew old he called his residence "Hidden Cliff", planted pines in the courtyard, and styled himself the "Seven-Pine Recluse".
translations.idiomatic: In old age he named his residence "Hidden Cliff", planted pines in the courtyard, and styled himself the "Seven-Pine Recluse".

sentences.zh: 敬晦，字日彰，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Jing Hui, courtesy name Rizhang, was a native of Hedong in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hui, whose courtesy name was Rizhang, was a native of Hedong in Hezhong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 祖括，字叔弓，進士及第，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuo, courtesy name Shugong, passed the jinshi examination and was transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuo, whose courtesy name was Shugong, passed the jinshi examination and rose to the post of Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠惡不諧己，外除果州刺史，進累兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong disliked him for not agreeing with him and had him sent out as Governor of Guo Prefecture; he was promoted in stages to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong resented his independence and had him sent out as Governor of Guo Prefecture; he was later promoted in stages to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 誌簡淡，在職不求名。

translations.literal: The record says he was simple and unassuming; in office he did not seek fame.
translations.idiomatic: Records describe him as plain and unassuming; in office he sought no renown.

sentences.zh: 周智光已誅，議者健括才，選為同州刺史，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: After Zhou Zhiguang had been executed, those in council praised Kuo's ability; he was selected as Governor of Tong Prefecture and appointed Censor in Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Zhiguang was executed, councilors praised Kuo's ability; he was chosen as Governor of Tong Prefecture and appointed Censor in Chief.

sentences.zh: 隱然持重，弗以私害公。

translations.literal: He was quietly dignified and steady, and never let private interest harm public duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was quietly dignified and steady, and never allowed private interest to compromise public duty.

sentences.zh: 大歷中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Dali reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Dali reign.

sentences.zh: 晦進士及第，辟山南東道節度府，與馬曙聯舍。

translations.literal: Hui passed the jinshi examination and was invited to the staff of the Shannan East Circuit military commission, sharing lodgings with Ma Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Hui passed the jinshi examination and joined the staff of the Shannan East Circuit military commission, where he shared lodgings with Ma Shu.

sentences.zh: 於是，帥不政，法制陵頹，曙引大吏廷責之。

translations.literal: At that time the commissioner did not govern; laws and institutions were in decay; Shu summoned a senior official and rebuked him in open court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the commissioner neglected governance, and laws and institutions were in decay; Shu summoned a senior official and publicly rebuked him in court.

sentences.zh: 吏負兼軍職，不引咎，走訴諸府。

translations.literal: The official, who also held a concurrent military title, would not accept blame and ran off to complain to various offices.
translations.idiomatic: The official, who also held a concurrent military title, refused to accept blame and ran off to lodge complaints with various offices.

sentences.zh: 牙將且十輩，方雜語以申吏枉，晦讓諸將曰：「吏冒軍名，公等不能詰，反引與為伍，奈何？」

translations.literal: Nearly ten military adjutants were just then talking together to plead the official's injustice; Hui reproached the commanders, saying, "This official falsely wears a military title, yet you cannot question him and instead take his part—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten garrison adjutants were then talking together to plead the official's case; Hui reproached the commanders, saying, "This official falsely wears a military title, yet you cannot question him and instead side with him—how can this be tolerated?"

sentences.zh: 眾愧謝，闔府咨美。

translations.literal: The crowd apologized in shame, and the whole commission praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The men apologized in shame, and the whole commission praised him.

sentences.zh: 擢累諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，趙歸真以詐營罔天子，御史平吳湘獄，得罪宰相。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wuzong's reign, Zhao Guizhen deceived the Son of Heaven through fraudulent machinations; the censorate settled the Wu Xiang case and offended the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wuzong's reign, Zhao Guizhen deceived the emperor through fraudulent schemes, and when the censorate settled the Wu Xiang case it offended the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 晦上疏極道非是，不少回縱。

translations.literal: Hui submitted a memorial vigorously stating that this was wrong and would not yield in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Hui submitted a memorial forcefully declaring the matter wrong and would not soften his position in the least.

sentences.zh: 大中中，歷御史中丞、刑部侍郎、諸道鹽鐵轉運使、浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he successively served as Vice Censor in Chief, Vice Minister of Justice, Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner for all circuits, and Observation Commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era he served successively as Vice Censor in Chief, Vice Minister of Justice, Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner for all circuits, and Observation Commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 時南方連饉，有詔弛榷酒茗，官用告覂，晦處身儉勤，貲力遂充。

translations.literal: At that time the south suffered successive famines; an edict relaxed the wine and tea monopolies, and government revenues were exhausted; Hui lived thriftily and diligently, and assets were thereby replenished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the south suffered successive famines; an edict relaxed the wine and tea monopolies, and government revenues were exhausted. Hui lived thriftily and diligently, and the commission's resources were restored.

sentences.zh: 徙兗州節度使，以太子賓客分司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Yan Prefecture, then served as Guest of the Heir Apparent at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Governor of Yan Prefecture, then served as Guest of the Heir Apparent with a nominal post at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部尚書，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of War, with the posthumous title Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of War, with the posthumous title Solemn.

sentences.zh: 晦兄昕、臯，弟戶、煦，俱第進士籍。

translations.literal: Hui's elder brothers Xin and Gao, and younger brothers Hu and Xu, all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's elder brothers Xin and Gao and his younger brothers Hu and Xu all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 昕為河陽節度使，臯右散騎常侍，世寵其家。

translations.literal: Xin became Military Governor of Heyang; Gao became Right Regular Attendant; for generations the court favored their family.
translations.idiomatic: Xin became Military Governor of Heyang, and Gao became Right Regular Attendant; for generations the court favored their family.

sentences.zh: 韋博，字大業，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Bo, courtesy name Daye, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo, whose courtesy name was Daye, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖黃裳，浙西節度觀察使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huangshang was Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huangshang had served as Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 博取進士第，浸遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Bo passed the jinshi examination and was gradually transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Bo passed the jinshi examination and gradually rose to the post of Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 開成中，蕭本詐窮得罪，詔與中人籍其財，中人利寶玉，欲竊取去，博奪還，簿無遺貲。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era, Xiao Ben's fraud was exposed and he was punished; an edict ordered Bo to inventory his property with eunuchs; the eunuchs coveted jewels and jade and tried to steal them away; Bo seized them back, and the ledger showed no missing property.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaicheng era, Xiao Ben's fraud was exposed and he was punished; an edict ordered Bo to inventory his property together with eunuchs. The eunuchs coveted his jewels and jade and tried to steal them, but Bo recovered everything, and the ledger showed no missing property.

sentences.zh: 回鶻入寇，以符澈為河東節度使，拜博為判官。

translations.literal: When the Uyghurs invaded, Fu Che was made Military Governor of Hedong, and Bo was appointed as his staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs invaded, Fu Che was appointed Military Governor of Hedong, and Bo was made a staff judge under him.

sentences.zh: 久之，進主客郎中。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 時詔毀佛祠，悉浮屠隸主客。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered the destruction of Buddhist temples, and all monks were placed under the Bureau of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict ordered the destruction of Buddhist temples, and all monks were placed under the Bureau of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 博言令太暴，宜近中，宰相李德裕惡之。

translations.literal: Bo said the order was too harsh and should be more moderate; the chancellor Li Deyu disliked him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Bo argued that the order was too harsh and should be more moderate; Chancellor Li Deyu took offense at this.

sentences.zh: 會羌、渾叛，以何清朝為靈武節度使，詔博副之，擢右諫議大夫，召對，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When the Qiang and Hun rebelled, He Qingchao was made Military Governor of Lingwu; an edict made Bo his deputy; he was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grand Master, summoned for audience, and granted the gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang and Hun rebelled, He Qingchao was appointed Military Governor of Lingwu, and Bo was ordered to serve as his deputy. He was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grand Master, summoned for audience, and granted the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 因行西北邊，商虜強弱，還奏有旨，進左大夫，為京兆尹。

translations.literal: He then traveled the northwest frontier, assessed the strength of the barbarians, and on returning submitted a memorial that received imperial approval; he was promoted to Left Grand Master and made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He then toured the northwest frontier, assessed the strength of the enemy tribes, and on returning submitted a memorial that received imperial approval. He was promoted to Left Grand Master and appointed Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 與御史中丞囂競不平，皆得罪，下除博衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He quarreled loudly and bitterly with the Vice Censor in Chief; both were punished, and Bo was demoted to Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled bitterly with the Vice Censor in Chief; both were punished, and Bo was demoted to Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 出為平盧節度使、檢校禮部尚書，徙昭義。

translations.literal: He went out as Military Governor of Pinglu with check only as Minister of Rites, then was transferred to Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Military Governor of Pinglu with nominal rank as Minister of Rites, then transferred to Zhaoyi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-two and was posthumously honored as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 李景讓，字後己，贈太尉憕孫也。

translations.literal: Li Jingrang, courtesy name Houji, was the grandson of the posthumously honored Grand Marshal Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingrang, whose courtesy name was Houji, was the grandson of the posthumously honored Grand Marshal Chong.

sentences.zh: 性方毅有守。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright, resolute, and principled.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright, resolute, and principled.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli reign he was transferred to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli reign he was transferred to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使王播以錢十萬市朝廷歡，求領鹽鐵，景讓詣延英亟論不可，遂知名。

translations.literal: Wang Bo, Military Governor of Huainan, offered one hundred thousand cash to buy the court's favor and sought to take charge of salt and iron; Jingrang went to Yan Ying Hall and urgently argued that this must not be allowed, and thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo, Military Governor of Huainan, offered one hundred thousand cash to buy favor at court and sought control of the salt and iron monopoly; Jingrang went to Yan Ying Hall and urgently argued against it, and thereby made his name.

sentences.zh: 沈傳師觀察江西，表以自副。

translations.literal: Shen Chuanshi, Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi, recommended him as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chuanshi, Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi, recommended him as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 歷中書舍人、禮部侍郎、商華虢三州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Secretariat Drafter, Vice Minister of Rites, and Governor of the three prefectures of Shang, Hua, and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Secretariat Drafter, Vice Minister of Rites, and Governor of Shang, Hua, and Guo Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 母鄭，治家嚴，身訓勒諸子。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Zheng, managed the household strictly and personally admonished and disciplined her sons.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zheng, ran the household with strict discipline and personally admonished and disciplined her sons.

sentences.zh: 始，貧乏時，治墻得積錢，僮婢奔告，母曰：「士不勤而祿，猶菑其身，況無妄而得，我何取？」

translations.literal: At first, when the family was poor, while repairing a wall they found a hoard of cash; servants ran to tell her; the mother said, "A scholar who receives salary without diligence already harms himself—how much more so unearned gain? Why should I take it?"
translations.idiomatic: When the family was still poor, they found a hoard of cash while repairing a wall, and the servants ran to tell her. His mother said, "A scholar who receives salary without diligence already harms himself—how much more so unearned gain? Why should I take it?"

sentences.zh: 亟使閉坎。

translations.literal: She immediately had the pit closed.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately had the pit closed up again.

sentences.zh: 景讓自右散騎常侍出為浙西觀察使，母問行日，景讓率然對：「有日。」

translations.literal: Jingrang went out from Right Regular Attendant to become Observation Commissioner of Zhexi; his mother asked the day of departure; Jingrang answered offhand, "There is a day."
translations.idiomatic: When Jingrang left his post as Right Regular Attendant to become Observation Commissioner of Zhexi, his mother asked when he would depart. Jingrang answered casually, "Soon."

sentences.zh: 鄭曰：「如是，吾方有事，未及行。」

translations.literal: Lady Zheng said, "If that is so, I have business of my own and am not yet ready to go."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng said, "If that is so, I have matters of my own to attend to and am not ready to go yet."

sentences.zh: 蓋怒其不嘗告也。

translations.literal: This was because she was angry that he had not informed her beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: She was angry that he had not told her beforehand.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「已貴，何庸母行？」

translations.literal: She also said, "You are already honored—why need your mother go?"
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "You are already a man of rank—why should your mother accompany you?"

sentences.zh: 景讓重請罪，乃赦。

translations.literal: Jingrang repeatedly begged forgiveness, and she then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang repeatedly begged forgiveness, and only then did she relent.

sentences.zh: 故雖老猶加箠敕，已起，欣欣如初。

translations.literal: Therefore even when he was old she still beat and admonished him; once he had risen, he was as cheerful as before.
translations.idiomatic: Even in old age she still beat and admonished him, yet once the punishment was over he was as cheerful as ever.

sentences.zh: 嘗怒牙將，杖殺之，軍且謀變，母欲息眾讙，召景讓廷責曰：「爾填撫方面而輕用刑，一夫不寧，豈特上負天子，亦使百歲母銜羞泉下！

translations.literal: Once in anger he had a military adjutant beaten to death; the army was about to mutiny; his mother, wishing to calm the soldiers' uproar, summoned Jingrang and rebuked him in open court, saying, "You govern a frontier region yet use punishment lightly; if one man is not at peace, do you not fail the Son of Heaven above and also make your hundred-year-old mother bear shame in the grave below!
translations.idiomatic: Once, in anger, he had a garrison adjutant beaten to death, and the army was on the verge of mutiny. To calm the uproar, his mother summoned Jingrang and publicly rebuked him, saying, "You govern a frontier region yet use punishment recklessly. If one man is not at peace, do you not fail the Son of Heaven above and also bring shame upon your hundred-year-old mother in the grave below!

sentences.zh: 何面目見先大夫乎？」

translations.literal: With what face can you meet your late father?"
translations.idiomatic: With what face can you meet your late father?"

sentences.zh: 將鞭其背，吏大將再拜請，不許，皆泣謝，乃罷，一軍遂定。

translations.literal: She was about to whip his back; the staff officers and senior commanders bowed twice and pleaded; she would not agree; all wept and apologized; then she stopped, and the whole army was settled.
translations.idiomatic: She was about to whip his back. The staff officers and senior commanders bowed twice and pleaded with her, but she would not relent until all wept and apologized. Only then did she stop, and the whole army was calmed.

sentences.zh: 景讓家行脩治，閨門唯謹。

translations.literal: Jingrang's family conduct was well ordered, and the inner household was exceedingly proper.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang's family conduct was exemplary, and his household was governed with the utmost propriety.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書左丞，拜天平節度使，徙山南東道，封酒泉縣男。
