translations.literal: He entered the capital as Left Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Military Governor of Tianping, was transferred to Shannan East Circuit, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiuquan County.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Left Assistant Minister, was appointed Military Governor of Tianping, was transferred to Shannan East Circuit, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiuquan County.

sentences.zh: 大中中，進御史大夫，甫視事，劾免侍御史孫玉汝、監察御史盧栯，威肅當朝。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he was promoted to Censor in Chief; as soon as he took office he impeached and removed Palace Censor Sun Yuru and Investigating Censor Lu Yi, and his authority awed the court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era he was promoted to Censor in Chief. As soon as he took office he impeached and removed Palace Censor Sun Yuru and Investigating Censor Lu Yi, and his authority awed the court.

sentences.zh: 為大夫三月，蔣伸輔政，景讓名素出伸右，而宣宗擇宰相，盡書群臣當選者，以名內器中，禱憲宗神禦前射取之，而景讓名不得。

translations.literal: After three months as Censor in Chief, Jiang Shen was assisting in government; Jingrang's reputation had always stood above Jiang Shen's, yet when Emperor Xuanzong chose a chancellor he wrote out all the ministers who should be selected, put the names in a vessel, prayed before Emperor Xianzong's spirit tablet and drew one by shooting at it, and Jingrang's name was not chosen.
translations.idiomatic: After three months as Censor in Chief, Jiang Shen was serving as chief minister. Jingrang's reputation had always stood above Jiang Shen's, yet when Emperor Xuanzong chose a chancellor he wrote out all the ministers eligible for selection, placed the names in a vessel, prayed before Emperor Xianzong's spirit tablet, and drew one by shooting at it—and Jingrang's name was not chosen.

sentences.zh: 世謂除大夫百日，有他官相者，謂之「辱臺」。

translations.literal: The world says that within a hundred days after appointment as Censor in Chief, if one receives another office equivalent to chancellor, it is called "disgracing the censorate".
translations.idiomatic: It was said that if, within a hundred days of appointment as Censor in Chief, one received another office equivalent to chancellor, this was called "disgracing the censorate".

sentences.zh: 景讓愧艴不能平，見宰相，自陳考深當代，即拜西川節度使。

translations.literal: Jingrang was ashamed and angry and could not be at peace; he saw the chancellor, stated that his qualifications ran deep in his generation, and was immediately appointed Military Governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang was ashamed and angry and could not rest; he saw the chancellor, declared that his qualifications were unmatched in his generation, and was immediately appointed Military Governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 以病丐致仕，或諫：「公廉潔亡素儲，不為諸子謀邪？」

translations.literal: Ill, he requested retirement; someone admonished him, saying, "You, sir, are honest and clean and have no savings—will you not plan for your sons?"
translations.idiomatic: When illness led him to request retirement, someone admonished him, saying, "You, sir, are honest and frugal and have no savings—will you not provide for your sons?"

sentences.zh: 景讓笑曰：「兒曹詎餓死乎？」

translations.literal: Jingrang smiled and said, "Would my sons ever starve to death?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang smiled and said, "Would my sons ever starve?"

sentences.zh: 書聞，輒還東都。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived, he at once returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived, he returned at once to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以太子少保分司。

translations.literal: He served as Senior Mentor to the Heir Apparent with a nominal post at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Senior Mentor to the Heir Apparent with a nominal post at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈太子太保，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two; posthumously he was made Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Filial.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Filial.

sentences.zh: 性獎士類，拔孤仄，如李蔚、楊知退皆所推引。

translations.literal: By nature he encouraged scholars, promoted obscure and disadvantaged men, and such men as Li Wei and Yang Zhitu were all advanced by him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he encouraged scholars and promoted obscure and disadvantaged men; Li Wei and Yang Zhitu were among those he advanced.

sentences.zh: 始為左丞，蔣伸坐宴所，酌酒語客曰：「有孝於家、忠於國者飲此。」

translations.literal: When he first became Left Assistant Minister, Jiang Shen was seated at a banquet; he poured wine and said to the guests, "Let whoever is filial at home and loyal to the state drink this."
translations.idiomatic: When Jingrang first became Left Assistant Minister, Jiang Shen was hosting a banquet. He poured wine and said to the guests, "Let whoever is filial at home and loyal to the state drink this."

sentences.zh: 客肅然，景讓起卒爵。

translations.literal: The guests were solemn; Jingrang rose and drained the cup.
translations.idiomatic: The guests fell silent; Jingrang rose and drained the cup.

sentences.zh: 伸曰：「無宜於公。」

translations.literal: Jiang Shen said, "None is more fitting than you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shen said, "No one is more fitting than you, sir."

sentences.zh: 所善蘇滌、裴夷直皆為李宗閔、楊嗣復所擢，故景讓在會昌時，抑厭不遷。

translations.literal: Those he favored, Su Di and Pei Yizhi, had all been promoted by Li Zongmin and Yang Sifu; therefore during the Huichang era Jingrang was suppressed and not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Those he favored, Su Di and Pei Yizhi, had all been promoted by Li Zongmin and Yang Sifu; for this reason Jingrang was suppressed and denied promotion during the Huichang era.

sentences.zh: 宣宗銜穆宗舊怨，景讓建請遷敬、文、武三主，以猶子行為嫌，請還代宗以下主復入廟，正昭穆。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong bore an old grudge against Emperor Muzong; Jingrang memorialized requesting the removal of the three emperors Jing, Wen, and Wu, objecting to the practice of adopting sons as heirs, and requested that the emperors from Daizong onward be returned to the main temple to correct the zhao-mu order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong still harbored old grievances against Emperor Muzong. Jingrang memorialized requesting the removal of Emperors Jing, Wen, and Wu from their positions, objecting to the practice of adopting sons as heirs, and asked that the emperors from Daizong onward be restored to the main temple to correct the zhao-mu order.

sentences.zh: 事下百官議，不然，乃罷，德望稍衰矣。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to all officials for discussion; they did not agree, and the proposal was dropped; his moral prestige gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to all officials for discussion; they did not agree, and the proposal was dropped. His moral prestige gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 然清素寡欲，門無雜賓。

translations.literal: Yet he was pure and simple, with few desires, and no miscellaneous guests at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remained pure and simple, with few desires, and admitted no unworthy guests to his gate.

sentences.zh: 李琢罷浙西，以同裏訪之，避不見；

translations.literal: When Li Zhuo left Zhexi he visited him as a fellow townsman; Jingrang avoided him and would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhuo left his post in Zhexi he came to visit as a fellow townsman, but Jingrang avoided him and refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 及去，命劚其騙石焉。

translations.literal: When Li Zhuo had gone, Jingrang ordered his inscribed stone removed.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Zhuo left, Jingrang ordered his inscribed stone dug up and removed.

sentences.zh: 元和後，大臣有德望者，以居裏顯，景讓宅東都樂和裏，世稱清德者，號「樂和李公」雲。

translations.literal: After the Yuanhe era, great ministers of moral prestige were known by the lane in which they lived; Jingrang's residence was in Lehe Lane in the Eastern Capital; those in the world who praised his pure virtue called him "Lord Li of Lehe".
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuanhe era, great ministers of moral prestige were known by the lane in which they lived. Jingrang's residence was in Lehe Lane in the Eastern Capital, and those who praised his pure virtue called him "Lord Li of Lehe".

sentences.zh: 弟景溫，字德己，歷諫議大夫、福建觀察使，徙華州刺史，以美政聞。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jingwen, courtesy name Deji, successively served as Remonstrating Grand Master and Observation Commissioner of Fujian, was transferred to Governor of Hua Prefecture, and was known for excellent governance.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jingwen, whose courtesy name was Deji, served successively as Remonstrating Grand Master and Observation Commissioner of Fujian, was transferred to Governor of Hua Prefecture, and was known for excellent governance.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to Right Assistant Minister.

sentences.zh: 盧攜當國，弟隱繇博士遷水部員外郎，材下資淺，人疾其冒，無敢繩，景溫不許赴省。

translations.literal: When Lu Xie held power, his younger brother Yin was transferred from Erudite to Vice Director in the Bureau of Waterways; his talent was inferior and his seniority shallow; people resented his presumption and none dared restrain him; Jingwen would not permit him to attend office.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xie held power, his younger brother Yin was transferred from Erudite to Vice Director in the Bureau of Waterways despite inferior talent and shallow seniority. People resented the presumption, but none dared restrain him; Jingwen refused to permit him to attend office.

sentences.zh: 時故事久廢，景溫既舉職，人皆韙其正。

translations.literal: At that time old precedents had long been neglected; once Jingwen performed his duty, everyone approved his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Old precedents had long been neglected, but once Jingwen performed his duty everyone approved his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 弟景莊，亦至顯官。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jingzhuang also reached a prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jingzhuang also rose to a prominent office.
